title: Sex differences in the genetic basis of human recombination within 190,000 parent-child pairs
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Meiotic recombination drives genetic diversity and chromosome segregation, yet the genetic factors governing variation in human recombination rates across studies remain poorly understood. Here, we analyze 112,144 maternal and 78,653 paternal meiosis events across four countries and identify 58 independent genomic regions (24 unique across phenotypes) associated with recombination frequency and location. These include six novel female-specific regions harboring genes linked to ovarian function and a seventh novel region linked to male recombination, with many loci demonstrating sex-dependent effects. The between-sex genetic correlation is 0.374 (0.072 SD). While DNA markers account for 30-40% of individual-level variation in recombination rate, previously known global modulators explain only 37.7% (2.7% SD) of this variation in females and 47.1% (3.8% SD) in males. We create a polygenic predictor that significantly predicts recombination rates in women and men after adjusting for age and birth year. Furthermore, female recombination correlates significantly with reproductive outcomes and aging, after adjusting for study ascertainment. In the largest meta-analysis to date of human meiotic recombination, these findings uncover novel sex-specific loci and clarify the polygenic architecture underlying meiotic variation.

title: Tuning Mass Transport through Pressure Modulation for Lithium-Mediated Nitrogen Reduction
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction (LiNRR) produces ammonia at ambient pressure and temperature, and gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) have advanced its production rate by intensifying nitrogen availability. However, the mass transport of lithium, nitrogen, and proton donor within the GDE and how the balance of their fluxes governs LiNRR performance remain underexplored. Here, we spatiotemporally varied the balance of species fluxes in a LiNRR GDE by dynamically modulating the pressure difference across the electrode, which altered the position of the gas/electrolyte interface. We found that decoupling the pressures applied during the plating and resting steps of pulsed electrolysis leads to higher ammonia production rates compared to the corresponding static pressure conditions. Decoupled pressure modulation enables even lithium plating during electrolysis and fast transport of nitrogen and proton donor during subsequent ammonia formation steps. This strategy may unlock a new design space for LiNRR by dynamically optimizing the reaction interface.

title: Transition from Dehydration to Rehydration of Chloride Salts near the Melting Point: Thermodynamic Origin and Implications for High-Temperature Corrosion
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molten chloride salts are promising functional media for high-temperature energy systems; however, trace water can accelerate corrosion of structural materials. We investigated changes in water concentration in six chloride salts—LiCl, NaCl, MgCl2, KCl, CaCl2, and ZnCl2—during heating across their solid-to-liquid phase transitions under a nominally inert Ar atmosphere. During solid-state heating, water concentration generally decreased, indicating dehydration. With further heating toward and through melting, however, this trend unexpectedly reversed in five salts except ZnCl2. As these salts entered the liquid phase, their water concentrations increased, marking a transition from dehydration to rehydration. Thermodynamic analysis showed that melting shifts the free energy balance toward water incorporation through enthalpic and entropic contributions. By comparing molten MgCl2 under conditions allowing or restricting entry of Ar gas, we identified trace water in the Ar atmosphere as the source of rehydration. Corrosion tests further showed rehydration substantially increased 316H stainless steel corrosion.

title: Donor–Acceptor Tuning Regulates Viologen Redox Behavior for Selective H2O2 Photosynthesis
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Regulating redox-active electron acceptors offers a strategy for directing multielectron photocatalysis beyond conventional charge-separation engineering. Here, we demonstrate substituent-controlled viologen redox regulation in pyrene–viologen porous organic polymers (PyVio-X) for selective H2O2 photosynthesis. Carbonyl functionalization (PyVio-CO) enhances donor–acceptor interactions and charge separation, while facilitating photoinduced viologen radical (V-N+•) formation. PyVio-CO achieves an H2O2 production rate of 1786 μmol g–1 h–1 in pure water under visible light and ambient air, with a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.25% and an apparent quantum yield of 4.95%. Mechanistic investigations support sequential O2 reduction involving ·O2– and *OOH intermediates, mediated by reversible V-N2+/V-N+• redox cycling. Enhanced two-electron O2 reduction selectivity and suppressed H2O2 decomposition further promote H2O2 accumulation. This work establishes substituent-controlled redox mediation as a molecular design principle for selective multielectron photocatalysis.

title: Dynamic plasmonic imaging of electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for charge-resolved multiplex biosensing
source: Science Advances
abstract: Multiplexed profiling of diverse biomarkers is essential for precision diagnostics, but remains challenging for label-free sensors because signals typically scale with analyte mass. Here, we present a dynamic plasmonic imaging platform based on electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for multiplexed, label-free quantification of nucleic acids, proteins, and small molecules within a unified sensing architecture. Size-encoded nanoparticles tethered to a plasmonic surface are electrically actuated to oscillate vertically within the evanescent field and tracked by distance-resolved surface plasmon resonance imaging. Molecular binding alters the effective surface charge of each nano-oscillator, modulating the electrostatic-driven forces and changing oscillation amplitude. This charge-to-motion transduction mechanism reduces dependence on molecular mass and enhances sensitivity for low–molecular weight analytes. This platform simultaneously detects microRNAs, proteins, and small molecules spanning a ∼300-fold molecular weight range within a single field of view. We further demonstrate multiplexed profiling of tumor-associated microRNAs in pretreated supernatants from patient-derived breast cancer cells across 24 clinical samples. Dynamic plasmonic nano-oscillators provide a scalable architecture for multiplex molecular diagnostics.

title: Highly Efficient Functionalization of hBN With Lithium Oxalate: A Multifunctional Platform for Composites, Ion Transport, and Spin Labeling
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional solid‐state materials are crucial for enabling safer and simpler lithium battery architectures. Here we report a scalable, solvent‐free mechanochemical strategy to overcome the chemical inertness of hexagonal boron nitride and produce (LBNCO), a lithium‐rich boron nitride nanostructure. High‐energy milling simultaneously exfoliates hBN and induces robust covalent oxalate functionalization, yielding a nanocrystalline lamellar compound with intrinsically incorporated lithium. LBNCO exhibits ionic conductivity, electronic insulation, and thermal stability exceeding . Additional mechanochemical processing enables further lithium enrichment without compromising chemical stability, allowing tunable ionic conductivity. By integrating ion transport, mechanical robustness, and thermal stability within a single material, LBNCO establishes a new platform for solid‐state lithium batteries and related technologies.

title: Quinone Carbonyl‐Functionalized Carbon Dots Enable Selective 2e − Oxygen Reduction for Benzyl Alcohol‐Assisted Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) is often limited by competing four‐electron reduction. Here, a precursor‐controlled series of carbon dots (CDs) is developed. The quinone‐associated carbonyl characteristics are systematically tuned by varying the resorcinol‐to‐catechol feed ratio. Across this chemically related series, spectroscopic and electrochemical changes in quinone‐associated surface chemistry correlate with photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production, with resorcinol‐derived CDs ( m ‐CDs) showing the highest activity. In a benzyl alcohol (BA)/ H 2 O biphasic system, BA serves as the reductive substrate, coupling its oxidation with O 2 reduction to H 2 O 2 . A plate‐type microchannel reactor delivers H 2 O 2 production rates of 17.71 and 54.19 mmol g −1 h −1 at 25 and 60°C, respectively, under 450 nm irradiation. In situ spectroscopy and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) show reversible light‐induced changes in carbonyl/oxygen‐containing surface states, and EPR features consistent with semiquinone‐type and ∙ OOH‐related species. Combined with the electrochemical and photocatalytic results, these observations support peroxide‐selective O 2 reduction and motivate a proposed quinone‐associated surface redox model that may involve proton and electron transfer. This work establishes a tunable CDs platform for probing and regulating quinone‐associated surface chemistry in photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production.

title: Machine‐Learning‐Guided Structural Design of Interlayer‐Confined PEI‐Based Composites for Superior Dielectric Energy Storage
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Structural design plays a pivotal role in enhancing the performance of composite materials for electrostatic energy storage, particularly in pulsed power systems operating under extreme conditions. Herein, guided by a sequential multi‐target machine learning (ML) framework, a series of polymer‐based nanocomposites with an interlayer‐confined architecture are fabricated, featuring two‐dimensional in‐plane network formed by interlaced Na 0.5 Bi 0.5 TiO 3 (NBT) nanofibers embedded into the polyetherimide (PEI) matrix. This strategy leverages NBT nanofibers to tailor the spatial electric field distribution via their high dielectric constant, while the fillers simultaneously suppress chain mobility and thereby reduce the matrix diffusivity to reinforce mechanical strength, collectively enhancing breakdown strength and polarization, and thus contributing to excellent electrostatic energy storage capacity. The resulting polymer composite showcases impressive energy storage performance (energy storage density U e = 11.08 J/cm 3 , energy storage efficiency η = 95.46%) and excellent high‐temperature performance ( U e = 5.32 J/cm 3 with η > 90.00%, 150°C), which are far superior to those of most advanced polymer‐based dielectrics reported recently. This work establishes an ML‐guided structural design strategy for next‐generation multilayer polymer dielectrics toward superior energy storage.

title: Multifunctional Thermo‐Electronic Smart Fabrics Integrating Radiative Cooling and Energy Harvesting for Self‐Powered Intelligent Perception
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable smart fabrics with integrated thermal regulation and energy autonomy represent a transformative advancement in next‐generation wearable technologies. However, achieving synergistic multifunctionality with a signal platform remains a significant challenge. Herein, we present a multifunctional thermal management and self‐powered smart fabric (TMSPF) that seamlessly integrates passive radiative cooling (PRC) and triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) through a rationally designed functional architecture. The unique all‐fiber structure enables TMSPF good breathability and self‐cleaning properties, thereby providing a dry and comfortable microenvironment for the wearer. Notably, benefiting from the excellent dielectric properties of BaTiO 3 and interconnected porous fiber architecture, the TMSPF achieves excellent PRC capability (a maximum cooling temperature of ∼18.9°C under direct sunlight and a maximum cooling power of 105.9 W m −2 at daytime), as well as enhanced triboelectric output (170 V, 977 mW m −2 ) and high sensitivity (88.72 V kPa −1 ), enabling applications in power supply and intelligent perception. Moreover, TMSPF demonstrates broad application prospects in personal thermal management and raindrop energy harvesting. This synergistic integration effectively addresses the intrinsic trade‐off between energy harvesting and thermal comfort in conventional wearables. This work provides valuable insights into the design and fabrication of next‐generation wearable electronics with integrated thermal and energy functionalities.

title: Ductile Polycrystalline AgCuSe With Preferred Orientation for High Power Density Flexible Thermoelectric Device
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The recently discovered ductile inorganic thermoelectric (TE) materials provide a promising solution for developing flexible TE devices with high output power density used in wearable electronics. However, the current ductile polycrystalline TE materials are still very rare. In this work, we show that engineering a polycrystal with a strong preferred orientation along the crystal plane with a high ratio of cleavage energy to slip barrier energy can convert it from brittle into ductile. Taking AgCuSe as a case study, via controlling the rolling temperature and speed during the hot‐rolling process, the polycrystalline AgCuSe with (0 k 0) preferred orientation is successfully obtained, which exhibits excellent ductility at room temperature. Likewise, the ductile AgCuSe retains the good TE performance of brittle AgCuSe, with the room‐temperature power factor (∼21.7 µW cm −1 K −2 ) much higher than the best flexible AgCuSe‐based materials reported before. By using the ductile polycrystalline AgCuSe, an ultrathin flexible cross‐plane π‐shaped TE device is developed to show a maximum normalized power density up to 46 µW cm −2 K −2 , a record‐high value in flexible thermoelectrics. This work not only provides a novel ductile TE material for flexible thermoelectrics, but also offers an alternative route to discover more ductile inorganic materials by using the anisotropic mechanical properties.

title: Fabrication of Tri‐Phase Lithium Alloy in Seconds via an Implosion‐Popcorn Reaction Toward Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Introducing non‐lithium components to fabricate lithium‐based alloy anodes has emerged as a paramount strategy to enhance the processability and stability of lithium metal batteries. However, conventional fabrication suffers from the sluggish wetting kinetics of lithium with non‐lithium components, inducing severe phase heterogeneity and component agglomeration. Herein, we report an ultrafast, spontaneous implosion‐popcorn reaction that explosively disintegrates centimeter‐scale precursor ingots into ultra‐fine particles within seconds, yielding a uniformly dispersed tri‐phase alloy with an interpenetrating network of Fe, Li 3 P, and Li. The as‐obtained lithium alloy exhibits a significantly enhanced Young's modulus and can be processed into different forms, including coatable slurries, self‐standing foils, and active powders. This fabrication method shifts from traditional passive alloying to an active, highly efficient, and homogenous approach. When used as an anode, the homogeneous Li/Fe/Li 3 P architecture facilitates interfacial Li‐ion transfer and regulates initial Li nucleation, thereby promoting dense and uniform Li growth and enabling a cycling lifespan of over 3000 h, together with improved full‐cell stability.

title: Light‐Assisted Anion Exchange Membrane Water and Seawater Electrolysis on a Core–Shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O Catalyst
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing solar energy to assist water and seawater electrolysis represents a promising strategy to reduce the energy input for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its development remains challenging due to limited integration between light‐responsive catalysts and membrane electrolyzer systems. Here, we report a hierarchical core–shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O catalyst that enables efficient light‐assisted hydrogen evolution and is directly interfaced with an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer. The Cu 2 O nanowire core serves as a light‐harvesting scaffold, while the Co‐P nanosheet shell provides active sites, collectively enabling strong light absorption, suppressed reflectivity, and efficient photothermal conversion with localized interfacial heating. The interfacial interaction between Co‐P and Cu 2 O facilitates catalytic kinetics, as supported by experimental analyses, while theoretical calculations reveal optimized charge redistribution and a reduced water dissociation barrier. Under one‐sun irradiation, the catalyst achieves overpotentials of 62 and 253 mV at 10 and 500 mA cm −2 , respectively, in 1 M KOH, with activity enhancement predominantly governed by photothermal effects. When integrated into a light‐assisted AEM electrolyzer, the Co‐P@Cu 2 O||NiFe LDH pair delivers efficient and durable overall water and seawater electrolysis at large current densities. This work establishes a viable strategy for coupling photothermal‐assisted electrocatalysis with membrane electrolyzer systems, advancing solar‐assisted hydrogen production from diverse water resources.

title: Breaking the Thermal Limits: Solvation Chemistry of Hydrogel Electrolytes for Extreme‐Temperature Stable Zinc‐Ion Batteries
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are promising candidates for safe and cost‐effective energy storage, yet their practical deployment across a wide temperature range is severely constrained by temperature‐dependent ion‐transport limitations and electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability. At low temperatures, sluggish Zn 2+ transport and desolvation promote concentration polarization and nonuniform Zn deposition, while elevated temperatures accelerate water‐induced parasitic reactions, corrosion, and interfacial degradation. Hydrogel electrolytes offer opportunities to address these challenges by regulating water activity, Zn 2+ solvation, ion transport, and interfacial mechanics within an integrated polymer network. This review systematically elucidates five representative design strategies: high‐entropy environments, water‐deficient hydrogels, deep eutectic solvent‐mediated regulation, zwitterionic networks, and nanofiller reinforcement, with particular emphasis on their effects on Zn 2+ coordination, water organization, transport kinetics, and interfacial stability. Quantitative solvation and kinetic descriptors, including coordination numbers, ion‐pair populations, diffusion coefficients, transference numbers, interaction energies, and activation energies, are compared to clarify how electrolyte structure influences performance at different temperatures. The advantages and limitations of the five strategies are further compared in relation to their applicable temperature‐dependent challenges. Finally, key priorities are discussed for temperature‐resolved solvation characterization, operando analysis, practical cell evaluation, and standardized thermal testing, providing guidance for the development of hydrogel electrolytes toward reliable wide‐temperature AZMBs.

title: Gradient‐Driven Spatial Relay in Titanium Oxynitride for Photocatalytic CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 Conversion
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to C 2 H 4 demands simultaneous management of light harvesting, proton supply, and C−C coupling, functions that are difficult to integrate on a single surface site. Here, we present a “surface‐subsurface spatial relay” strategy to overcome this limitation using a gradient titanium oxynitride (G−TiNO) architecture that spatially partitions these steps, realizing CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 conversion without noble metal on Ti‐based catalysts. Operando spectroscopy and DFT reveal that the surface Ti−O layer captures CO 2 and dissociates water to supply *H, while a built‐in electric field drives linear intermediates into a subsurface N−Ti−O domain, where the barrier for *OCCO formation is markedly lowered. Crucially, operando XAFS spectroscopy unveils a reversible “breathing‐mode” adsorption of CO 2 within the gradient architecture, wherein the N−Ti−O lattice dynamically expands and contracts in response to interfacial charge accumulation, stabilizing key intermediates. The optimized G−TiNO−425 achieves a C 2 H 4 evolution rate of 73.34 µmol g −1 h −1 with 76.46% product selectivity and 93.14% electron selectivity. Comparative control experiments show that progressive removal of the TiNO interlayer shifts selectivity from C 2 H 4 to CO, establishing a causal link between the gradient interface and C−C coupling. This work provides a design principle for buried interfaces that exploit dynamic structural flexibility to direct complex multi‐electron photocatalysts.

title: Proton Competition Induced Stabilization in TEMPO‐Based Redox‐Targeting Flow Batteries
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT 2,2,6,6‐tetramethylpiperidine‐1‐oxyl (TEMPO) derivatives are widely studied as positive electrolytes in aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) due to their high redox potential. However, TEMPO‐based AORFBs suffer from stability issues with molecule degradation. In this work, a unique stabilization strategy beyond molecular engineering is developed by designing a TEMPO‐based redox‐targeting (RT) flow battery via a proton‐competition mechanism. A RT flow battery is constructed with 4‐acetamido‐TEMPO as redox mediator and polyaniline (PANI) as the solid material, achieving 4.37‐fold enhancement in capacity (35.72 Ah L −1 ), high coulombic efficiency (99.99%) and excellent capacity retention (99.94% per cycle over 500 cycles within 840.82 h). The outstanding stability of the TEMPO‐based flow battery is attributed to the synergistic interaction between proton buffering and RT reactions. This study elucidates a key pathway for suppressing TEMPO radical hydrogenation through a proton competition mechanism, which relies on the reversible doping/de‐doping cycles of the PANI. Operando spectroscopic studies and density functional theory calculations elucidate the mechanism, revealing an intermediate transition state and confirming that proton competition by PANI is pivotal for radical stabilization. This work delves into the mechanism of TEMPO‐based RT flow battery, providing design principles for advancing stable AORFB systems toward long‐duration energy storage applications.

title: Low-power Charge-domain In-FeRAM Computing
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The growing energy demands of large-scale model training and scientific computing have inspired interest in low-power computing paradigms. In-memory computing (IMC) reduces data movement overheads, but resistive devices suffer from high static power and Joule-heating. Here, we introduce a charge-domain computing paradigm based on Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 ferroelectric random-access memory (HZO FeRAM), in which computation is enabled by linear accumulation of charge associated with the anti-orientated ferroelectric polarization. We experimentally demonstrate this concept using a 16-kbit HZO FeRAM array, where key computational characteristics execute directly within this array, gradient calculations are performed with errors below 6×10 − 3, and in-memory difference operations solve partial differential equations with 98% accuracy after only 21 iterations. Hybrid FeRAM-digital training of a single-layer neural network for letter recognition is also shown. Furthermore, a 1 μm2 HZO ferroelectric capacitor exhibits a measured switching energy of only 1.66×10 − 12 J, implying the potential of HZO FeRAM for energy-efficient charge-domain computing.

title: Declining environmental predictability erodes reproduction in a tropical seabird
source: Nature Climate Change
abstract: Seasonal breeders often depend on predictable resource pulses, yet climate change may alter reliability without shifting average timing. Here, using satellite chlorophyll records and two decades of individual breeding data for a tropical seabird, we show that weakened breeding synchrony and declining and less consistent reproductive success were associated with increasingly variable bloom timing without a consistent directional shift. Focusing on average timing alone could mean that climate impacts on species are overlooked. The authors show that, for a tropical seabird model species, winter–spring phytoplankton blooms kept a stable mean timing but became more variable between years. Breeding synchrony weakened and reproductive success declined and became less consistent over the same two decades.

title: Sabatier Principle‐Guided Co‐Solvent Selection for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zinc Batteries
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic co‐solvents can effectively stabilize Zn anodes in rechargeable aqueous batteries, yet their selection remains largely empirical. Here, a Sabatier principle‐analogous framework utilizing molecular polarity index (MPI) as a quantitative descriptor is proposed for rational electrolyte engineering. By investigating a series of C3 alcohol co‐solvents with tunable hydroxyl configurations, we reveal a volcano‐type relationship between MPI and electrochemical performance. Co‐solvents with intermediate MPI, exemplified by 1,3‐propanediol, reside at the apex of this volcano. This optimal polarity strikes a delicate balance between interfacial homogeneity and reaction kinetics, thereby promoting dendrite‐free deposition and suppressing side reactions. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables a symmetric battery to achieve a cumulative plating capacity of 5.2 A h cm −2 and a lifespan exceeding seven months. Furthermore, a high‐mass‐loading (∼30 mg cm −2 ) Zn//I 2 pouch cell (0.3 A h) maintains stable operation over 1200 cycles with a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.057‰ per cycle. More importantly, this framework successfully identifies 1,2,4‐butanetriol as a new highly efficient co‐solvent, demonstrating the robust predictive power of MPI descriptor. This work translates the Sabatier principle into a predictive tool for electrolyte formulation, establishing a generalizable framework for co‐solvent screening that accelerates the development of high‐performance Zn batteries for large‐scale energy storage.

title: Magnetic‐Field Modulation of Oxygen Evolution at Structurally Constrained Single‐Atom Sites With a Secondary Photoresponse
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  External physical fields have emerged as promising tools for dynamically regulating electrocatalytic reactions, yet how different stimuli influence catalysis within structurally constrained active sites remains poorly understood. We establish structurally constrained Ni single‐atom‐anchored CdS as a model platform to investigate magnetic‐field modulation of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and its relationship to the photoresponse. Operando electrochemical measurements, quasi in situ spectroscopic characterizations, magnetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations reveal fundamentally distinct response pathways. The photo‐induced response is strongly potential‐dependent, with a clear photocurrent response at lower bias, but little additional current under strongly anodic OER conditions. In contrast, magnetic fields regulate the electronic structure of Ni active sites by modifying Ni 3d–S 3p orbital coupling and spin configurations, thereby reducing the free‐energy requirement for the potential‐determining *OH‐to‐*O conversion step without inducing significant changes in the coordination environment. Notably, the catalytic and spin responses observed under magneto‐optical conditions closely resemble those induced by magnetic fields alone, indicating that magnetic‐field‐driven spin regulation dominates OER kinetics in structurally constrained single‐atom active sites. This work demonstrates that different external fields access distinct electronic degrees of freedom and establishes a conceptual framework for external‐field‐regulated electrocatalysis beyond conventional structure‐based catalyst design.

title: Highly Efficient Organic Scintillators With Low Detection Limits via Cascade Energy Transfer in TADF‐Sensitized Fluorescence
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic scintillators have experienced notable advancements in performance, garnering considerable attention and demonstrating promising potential for diverse applications. However, an ideal scintillator requires efficient radiation absorption, rapid radiative decay, excellent stability, and a high light yield; it still remains challenging to simultaneously fulfill these criteria for a single organic material. Here, we propose to fabricate energy transfer cascade organic scintillators based on the TADF‐sensitized fluorescence (TSF) mechanism, in which the functions of x‐ray energy absorption, triplet exciton up‐conversion, and singlet exciton radiative transition are decoupled by three components cooperating to break through intrinsic shackles. As a result, a highlight output of 28.90 times that of anthracene crystal, a record detection limit as low as 17.69 nGy

                    were achieved. This work validates the universality and potential of the TSF mechanism to boost the performance of organic scintillators and is expected to advance the rapid development of organic scintillators.

title: Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity
source: Science Advances
abstract:
The multidomain scaffold RIM (Rab3-interacting molecule) is widely viewed as a broadly required organizer of the presynaptic active zone, clustering voltage-gated Ca
                    2+
                    (Ca
                    v
                    2) channels, priming synaptic vesicles, and supporting neurotransmitter release. Whether this reliance is uniform across synapses with distinct release probabilities, however, has been difficult to resolve at convergent inputs. Here, using neurotoxin-based silencing to isolate transmission at the
                    Drosophila
                    neuromuscular junction, we show that the requirement for RIM is highly input-specific: RIM is essential to empower transmission at a high–release probability phasic synapse, yet is largely dispensable at a neighboring low–release probability tonic synapse. This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. Super-resolution imaging reveals that RIM is positioned closer to Ca
                    v
                    2 channels at phasic synapses and, during acute plasticity, coordinates their nanoscale reorganization to drive the rapid expansion of the readily releasable pool.

title: 4D‐Printed Intelligent Electromagnetic Materials for Adaptive Microwave Stealth and Multispectral Camouflage
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Increasingly complex and dynamic applications demand intelligent and adaptive electromagnetic (EM) stealth and multispectral camouflage materials with self‐perception, actuation, and regulation capabilities. However, currently available EM materials with predesigned structure and confined EM performances cannot satisfy the diverse dynamic requirements. Herein, we report a general strategy to engineer intelligent reconfigurable EM materials by encoding programmable structures into liquid crystal elastomers with functional coating by topological 4D printing. The stimulus‐response structural reconfiguration establishes distinct EM‐wave interaction regimes and expands the accessible design space for EM functions, enabling the adaptive modulation of EM characteristics and multispectral camouflage. The proposed hypothesis is validated by constructing different reconfigurable structures with versatile functions. For example, the Miura‐origami configuration undergoes spontaneous folding under external stimuli, delivering reversible and seamless modulation from total reflection to broadband absorption (4.49–18 GHz, −21.4 dB). Moreover, reversible and adaptive switching between signal transmission and electromagnetic interference shielding is also achieved via a flower‐shaped “quasi‐Faraday cage”. Combined with outer functional coatings, it affords multispectral camouflage in dynamic and complex environments. Therefore, this work offers a feasible and versatile design route to develop reliable and self‐adaptive microwave stealth and multispectral camouflage materials for next‐generation intelligent systems.

title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
source: Science Advances
abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body–irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch
                    +
                    selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H
                    +
                    . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

title: Dynamics of excess renewable energy and implications for its potential use
source: Joule
abstract: Due to wind and solar variability, excess renewable energy could be available, even in systems with substantial storage. Across a wide range of possible systems, excesses typically occur in the afternoon and in spring and fall and persist for up to 7–12 h. Flexible technologies could be designed to utilize these excesses.

title: Plasmonic S‐Scheme Heterojunction‐Mediated Photocatalytic Cascade Reaction for Antibiotic Wastewater‐to‐Hydrocarbon Fuel Conversion
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocatalytic mineralization of organic pollutants has attracted considerable attention in antibiotic wastewater treatment. However, this process inevitably produces CO
                    2
                    , and the efficient treatment and utilization of this environmentally detrimental substance remain a major challenge. Herein, we demonstrate a photocatalytic cascade reaction on a well‐designed plasmonic S‐scheme heterojunction, where plasmonic W
                    18
                    O
                    49
                    acts as the oxidative photocatalyst for antibiotic mineralization into CO
                    2
                    , and amino‐rich g‐C
                    3
                    N
                    4
                    serves as the reductive photocatalyst to capture the as‐produced CO
                    2
                    and hydrogenate it into CO and CH
                    4
                    . This cascade reaction directly converts antibiotic‐contaminated wastewater into hydrocarbon fuels, thereby reducing CO
                    2
                    emissions. We show that visible‐NIR‐driven hot electrons in W
                    18
                    O
                    49
                    transfer to g‐C
                    3
                    N
                    4
                    to boost CO
                    2
                    hydrogenation, while the remaining holes sufficiently oxidize water into
                    ·
                    OH. Upon simulated sunlight irradiation, this process enhances the cascade reaction activity. With 5 mg of the S‑scheme heterojunction under 2 h irradiation, ∼86% tetracycline was degraded, lowering the initial wastewater toxicity. The carbon conversion efficiencies for tetracycline‐to‐CO/CH
                    4
                    and mineralization‑derived CO
                    2
                    ‐to‐CO/CH
                    4
                    reached ∼0.60% and ∼2.68%, respectively. This work provides a promising strategy for integrating pollutant degradation with CO
                    2
                    valorization via rational design of high‐performance photocatalysts, advancing sustainable wastewater treatment and carbon neutrality.

title: Direct Visualization of Polarity‐Driven Carrier Redistribution in Two‐Dimensional In/CdS
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The intrinsic polarization field (IPF) in wurtzite semiconductors has long been proposed as a means to regulate carrier migration in photocatalytic and optoelectronic systems. However, direct experimental visualization of polarity‐driven charge separation remains challenging because intrinsic polarization effects are often obscured by competing surface fields and structural heterogeneity, leading to long‐standing contradictions between theory and experiment. Here, we fabricate well‐defined two‐dimensional In‐doped CdS single‐crystalline flakes (In/CdS) with exposed polar basal planes, providing a model platform to directly probe polarity‐driven carrier redistribution. Kelvin probe force microscopy, combined with photo‐deposition and single‐molecule fluorescence imaging, reveals opposite carrier accumulation on the two basal surfaces of individual flakes, with the upper surface serving as an electron‐rich reduction site and the bottom surface acting as a hole‐rich oxidation site. The spatially separated carrier distribution enables selective co‐catalyst loading on electron‐accumulated surfaces and boosts photocatalytic H
                    2
                    evolution. Ultrafast spectroscopy reveals a long lifetime (>2 µs) of photogenerated electrons and ultrafast electron transfer to co‐catalysts with an efficiency approaching unity. This work provides long‐sought experimental proof of charge separation in polar semiconductors and establishes a paradigm for exploiting intrinsic bulk properties through 2D geometry.

title: Three‐Dimensional Topological Spin Textures Above Room Temperature in NdCo 3 Magnet
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Recently, topological spin configurations, such as skyrmions, (anti)merons, and hopfions, have garnered attention because of their scientific importance and potential industrial applications. However, systematically investigating their three‐dimensional (3D) spatial arrangements is essential for understanding their external‐field responses and enabling their practical use. Such investigations remain challenging owing to technical limitations. Herein, we report a comprehensive investigation of the 3D spin configurations in the centrosymmetric rare‐earth magnet NdCo
                    3
                    , revealing spontaneous composite stripe‐(anti)merons and dipolar skyrmions across a broad temperature range of 256–378 K. We resolved the random chirality of the (anti)merons by integrating in situ Lorentz transmission electron microscopy (L‐TEM), off‐axis electron holography, neutron diffraction, and micromagnetic simulations, and quantified their finite penetration depths. Furthermore, the dipolar skyrmions were shown to possess depth‐dependent spin textures, evolving from Néel‐type magnetization at the surfaces to Bloch‐type rotation in the intermediate layers. Our results establish NdCo
                    3
                    as a robust platform for high‐temperature 3D topological spin textures in centrosymmetric magnets and provide a general experimental–theoretical framework for reconstructing and controlling 3D spin textures in other topological magnetic systems.

title: Drug‐Stiffened Polymer Worms: Allostery‐Inspired Activity Gating and Endogenous Enzyme‐Recharged Catalytic Cycling
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural enzymes achieve efficient and specific catalysis through precise allosteric regulation, a dynamic interplay of conformational rigidity and flexibility that remains largely unrealized in synthetic catalysts. Here, we report an allostery‐inspired polymer assembly whose catalytic and therapeutic functions are gated by programmable changes in supramolecular rigidity. The assemblies initially form flexible worm‐like micelles, whereas drug loading induces coordination‐driven crystallization into rigid nanorods. This rigidification restricts substrate accessibility and electron transfer, concurrently suppressing its peroxidase‐like activity, drug cytotoxicity, and fluorescence. In the glutathione (GSH)‐rich tumor microenvironment, disruption of metal coordination reverses rigidification, restores the flexible morphology, and reactivates all functions. The activated assemblies then use tumor‐overexpressed NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) as an endogenous redox partner, channeling reducing equivalents from reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) to replenish their electron reservoir and enable repeated catalytic turnover. This NQO1‐recharged cascade depletes intracellular GSH and NADH while generating cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals, thereby inducing apoptosis, ferroptosis, and cuproptosis, triggering immunogenic cell death, and eliciting robust antitumor immunity in vivo. By integrating allostery‐inspired structure gating with endogenous‐enzyme‐driven catalyst recharging, this work establishes an adaptive catalytic platform that addresses limitations in the activity regulation and redox cycling of artificial enzymes and offers a strategy for catalytic cancer therapy.

title: Chain‐Regulated Degradation of Polyvinyl Chloride in UiO‐Type Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Converting polyvinyl chloride (PVC) into valuable hydrocarbons is hindered by rapid dehydrochlorination, which produces mainly coke and HCl and limits global recycling to below 8%. Existing strategies activate specific bonds but overlook chain regulation. Here we show that regulating PVC chains within the sub‐nanometer channels of UiO‐type metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) redirects degradation from uncontrolled elimination to size‐selective chain scission. In Zr‐based UiO‐66 and UiO‐67, periodic acidic Zr clusters anchor PVC through Zr─Cl bonds, inducing heterolytic C─Cl cleavage and β‐scission of carbocationic intermediates. The yield of volatile hydrocarbons increases from <5 wt% for bulk PVC degradation to ∼30 wt% for degradation in the MOF. The aliphatic chain length is governed by the MOF geometry‐dictated anchoring spacing (
                    γ
                    ): UiO‐66 (
                    γ
                    = 8 C─C bonds) favours C9 hydrocarbons, whereas UiO‐67 (
                    γ
                    = 10) favours C11 hydrocarbons. Molecular dynamics, thermodynamic calculations, and statistical kinetic modelling reveal that
                    γ
                    and carbocation‐mediated scission events control the carbon number of the products. This work establishes chain regulation as a design principle for controlling polymer degradation.

title: Evolutionarily reinforced GC-rich motif enables non-AUG translation in mammals under eIF1/5MP-mediated fidelity control
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Non-AUG translation contributes to proteome diversity, but its regulatory principles remain unclear. Here, we show that a GCC-rich upstream extension, termed the
                    NAT1
                    motif, acts as a potent enhancer of near-cognate initiation in mammals. Cell-free and reporter assays revealed that eIF1 and 5MP act as conserved inhibitors of non-AUG initiation across mammals and plants, while the
                    NAT1
                    motif enables enhanced initiation within this fidelity framework. Mutational analysis identified −6 and −7 positions within the GCC repeat as key determinants of motif activity. Genome-wide analyses uncovered evolutionary depletion of
                    NAT1
                    -type non-AUG codons in human 5′UTRs, suggesting purifying selection against excessive initiation. Nevertheless, more than a hundred retained sites are associated with genes involved in cell proliferation and migration, suggesting that regulated non-AUG initiation may contribute to disease-relevant translational programs. The motif’s enrichment within GCC repeats further suggests a mechanistic link to repeat-associated non-AUG translation.

title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on‐body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio‐signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular‐level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device‐level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device‐level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of an SP without incorporating soft segments into the backbone. This strategy promotes conformational flexibility and suppresses side‐chain interdigitation, enhancing chain dynamics and amplifying mechanical contrast between crystalline and amorphous domains. This facilitates localized stress accommodation and induces the formation of nano‐to‐micro scale crack clusters, termed artificial stretch marks (ASMs), which emulate the adaptive mechanical behavior of human skin. Leveraging this mechanism, ISOSTs maintain 83.8% of maximum current even under 150% strain while preserving synaptic behaviors. Furthermore, physical reservoir computing using the ISOSTs preserves electromyography classification performance under 150% tensile strain. This work presents a biomimetic stress dissipation strategy for intrinsically stretchable and stress‐adaptive neuromorphic electronics.

title: Dynamic Interfacial S–O Bonding Stabilizes Oxygen Redox Through Reversible Electron Confinement
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The reversible activation of lattice oxygen represents a transformative opportunity for high‐energy battery electrodes but remains fundamentally limited by the instability of oxidized oxygen states. In layered oxide cathodes, oxygen oxidation generates oxygen‐centered hole states that become electronically unstable at particle surfaces, triggering oxygen loss, interfacial reconstruction, and irreversible electrochemical degradation. Here, we develop an interfacial electronic regulation strategy that stabilizes oxygen redox through reversible sulfur–oxygen (S–O) bonding. During charging, dynamic S–O bond formation at the cathode surface confines oxygen hole states and suppresses their delocalization and irreversible evolutions, whereas bond dissociation upon discharge restores the lattice oxygen electronic configuration and enables reversible oxygen redox. Applied to the Na
                    0.72
                    Li
                    0.24
                    Mn
                    0.76
                    O
                    2
                    layered oxide cathode, this strategy enables stable oxygen redox activity, mitigates voltage decay, and improves long‐term cycling stability. These findings establish reversible interfacial electron confinement as a general design principle for regulating unstable oxygen electronic states and advancing durable high‐energy‐storage materials.

title: Colloidal Photonic Crystals Toward Scalable Manufacturing and Reliable Functions
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Colloidal photonic crystals (CPCs) have attracted considerable attention because of their specific optical properties and versatile structural functionality. While previous reviews have extensively covered the fundamental design and fabrication principles of functional CPCs, a systematic perspective on their transitioning from laboratory‐scale demonstrations to scalable manufacturing remains less explored. In this review, we therefore specifically fill this gap by summarizing recent advances on colloidal assembly, structural evolution, and stabilization strategies relevant to large‐scale fabrication and application‐oriented use. First, a concise overview of refining the classification of building blocks is provided for establishing a library to construct well‐defined periodic sophisticated photonic nanostructures. Second, we discuss scalable assembly from the perspective of processing constraints on how mild conditions, short assembly times, simplified procedures, and large‐area uniformity can be balanced. This is followed by discussing structural color modulation beyond stimulus‐based classification, and design strategies that enhance color fidelity, mechanical stability, and robustness. Emerging applications of these unique photonic systems, including anti‐counterfeiting, sensing, displays, and bio‐related devices, are highlighted. Finally, this review presents some challenges and perspectives on the development of colloid‐based scalable photonic materials, aiming to provide a scientific framework for bridging laboratory‐scale photonic materials with industrial‐scale manufacturing and reliable functions.

title: Number of international students arriving in US plunges — worrying scientists
source: Nature
abstract: Declines in students from China and India are driving the trend, which researchers say could slow the progress of US science.

title: 2DIR hyperspectral imaging of polariton propagation reveals fewer dark modes per polariton
source: Chem
abstract: Change in chemical reactions under strong coupling with confined electromagnetic cavities has been previously experimentally observed. However, theoretically, the number of molecules per cavity mode is too high to explain the experiment. In this work, the authors experimentally measure this number, and find that it is much smaller than assumed, using 2DIR imaging and, thus, lay the foundation for better understanding polariton phenomena and future system design.

title: H-aggregated supramolecular packing lowers exciton binding energy for efficient quinone-phenol-mediated H2O2 photosynthesis
source: Chem
abstract: Controlling how molecules assemble provides a powerful route to regulate the fate of photoexcited states. H-type packing strengthens intermolecular electronic delocalization, weakens exciton binding, and promotes charge generation in perylene diimide (PDI) supramolecules, enabling efficient solar H2O2 photosynthesis. This work establishes supramolecular packing as a molecular design strategy for exciton management and solar-to-chemical energy conversion.

title: Streets of glass
source: Nature Cities
abstract: Through the glass pavement lights embedded in Dublin’s streets, this I and the City explores how memory, politics and everyday movement are inscribed in the city’s material fabric.

title: Photoenzymatic control of phosphorus radicals
source: Nature Catalysis
abstract: Photoenzymatic catalysis has enabled an increasingly diverse range of asymmetric radical transformations, yet phosphorus-centred radicals have remained beyond its reach. Engineered enzymes now enable stereoselective hydrophosphinylation, including products bearing carbon stereocentres, phosphorus stereocentres, or both.

title: Boron‐Stabilized Diradicaloids of Chichibabin and Müller Hydrocarbons and Their Extended Analogues
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Boron incorporation provides an effective strategy for stabilizing organic open‐shell radicals while simultaneously modulating their electronic structures and properties. Herein, we report a series of boron‐containing Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids featuring linearly extended π‐conjugated backbones and terminal triarylborane units. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that elongation of the conjugated bridges progressively weakens the interaction between two spin centers, leading to increased diradical character from 0.53 to 0.99, and narrowing the singlet–triplet energy gap from –3.42 to –2.58 kcal mol
                    ‒1
                    . Despite their strong open‐shell nature, these organoboron diradicaloids exhibit remarkable stability, with half‐life time exceeding 40 days, owing to effective spin‐stabilization by the vacant p orbitals of the boron centers. They display backbone‐dependent aromaticity, tunable near‐infrared absorption, and reversible four‐electron redox behavior. Two‐electron chemical reduction affords the corresponding closed‐shell dianionic species with distinct aromatic reorganization and progressively red‐shifted fluorescence from 581 to 656 nm. These results thus establish a versatile boron‐based approach to stabilizing and tuning Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids, providing new opportunities for the development of heterocyclic diradicaloid chemistry and functional open‐shell materials.

title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Alkyl carboxylic acids are fundamental building blocks in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. The direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO
                    2
                    offers an atom‐economical route to these valuable compounds, avoiding prefunctionalized substrates and harsh reaction conditions. However, the inherently negative reduction potentials of both unactivated alkenes and CO
                    2
                    pose substantial barriers to their direct transformation. To date, most electrochemical hydrocarboxylation methods are restricted to activated alkenes, as these substrates can form stabilized intermediates that facilitate the reaction. In sharp contrast, the hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes remains a formidable challenge, largely due to their electronic neutrality and the lack of efficient pathways to stabilize the key intermediates. Herein, we report a direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes under transition metal‐ and base‐free conditions. This protocol not only maximizes atom utilization, but also accommodates a broad range of substrates, including sensitive halides, esters,
                    N
                    ‐heterocycles, and even synthetically challenging 1,1‐disubstituted unactivated alkyl alkenes. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the preparation of value‐added products, such as monomethyl adipate and undecanoic acid. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and radical ring‐opening experiments, support the generation of the CO
                    2
                    radical anion and its subsequent selective radical addition to the unactivated C═C bond.

title: Chinese graduate students are now choosing to stay closer to home

abstract: Malaysia, Hong Kong and Macau are the new hot destinations for students.

title: Automated Flow Synthesis of Combinatorial Protein‐Length Polyamide Libraries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Flow synthesis with building block mixtures permits the generation of hypervariable polyamide libraries with up to quintillions (10
                    18
                    ) of sequence‐defined compounds per pooled mixture on a timescale of < 1 h per synthesis. The semi‐automated flow platform on which we have previously developed this technique, however, lacks the efficiency required to make protein‐length polyamide chains. To facilitate the direct engraftment of variable regions into longer polyamide chains, we adapted mixture‐based library synthesis to automated flow peptide synthesis (AFPS) systems previously optimized for the production of 100‐200‐mer synthetic proteins. Using this approach, we demonstrate the single‐shot synthesis of a 101‐mer model library with empirically estimated content approaching quintillions of members composed of both L‐ and D‐amino acid building blocks. AFPS thus permits the incorporation of hypervariable polyamide libraries into synthetic protein‐length polyamide scaffolds, expanding accessible combinatorial space in protein‐length synthetic chains by orders of magnitude while retaining synthetic control for application to affinity selection‐mass spectrometry workflows.

title: Ribo@DNA: Ribonucleotides as Convenient Handles for Site‐Specific DNA Conjugation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  DNA conjugates are broadly enabling in biotechnology and medicine, yet methods for synthesizing many of these conjugates are often complex and expensive. Here we report the use of ribonucleotides locally incorporated within DNA oligonucleotides (ribo@DNA) as reactive handles for facile, high‐yield post‐synthesis conjugation in water. The site of reaction is the 2′‐OH group of the ribonucleotide, which is selectively nucleophilic in aqueous solution toward acyl, sulfonyl, and aryl electrophiles. Mass spectrometry data document that the reactions occur in moderate to high conversions with all four ribonucleotides, establishing sequence and positional versatility. Side products are chiefly the result of over‐modification in cases of highly reactive or bulky reagents (ca. 0%–15%). The crude modified oligodeoxynucleotide can be isolated by precipitation, or can be purified readily by high performance liquid chromatography. Examples are documented of incorporation of varied acyl groups with alkanoyl or aroyl structure, sulfonyl groups, aryl groups, clickable residues, fluorophores, and reversible groups. Conjugation reactions at 2′‐O with carboxylic acids, thiols, amines, aryl halides, and alcohols are demonstrated, resulting in broadly varied functional linkages including ethers, esters, carbamates, carbonates, and thiocarbonates. This strategy offers an inexpensive and exceptionally versatile alternative to nucleobase conjugates for modification of DNA.
