title: Spin Transport in Epitaxial Magnon Junctions With Pt‐Nanoparticle‐Decorated Y 3 Fe 5 O 12 /Gd 3 Ga 5 O 12 /Y 3 Fe 5 O 12
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The excitation, propagation, manipulation, and detection of magnons are central to magnonics. High‐quality ferromagnetic insulator (FI)/antiferromagnetic insulator (AFI)/ferromagnetic insulator (FI) magnon junctions are predicted to achieve nearly 100% magnon junction ratio (MJR), making them attractive for non‐volatile spintronic/magnonic devices. However, lattice‐mismatched AFI spacers generally disrupt the epitaxial growth of the top low‐damping yttrium iron garnet (Y
                    3
                    Fe
                    5
                    O
                    12
                    , YIG) layer, degrading its crystalline quality and limiting magnon transmission. Here, we demonstrate that Pt‐nanoparticle decoration enables fully epitaxial magnon junctions with a well‐defined antiparallel magnetic configuration. The incorporated Pt nanoparticles enhance the coercivity of the top YIG layer while preserving its high crystalline quality and low magnetic damping. A clear magnon junction effect is observed, yielding an intrinsic MJR of 23% extracted by peak analysis. Besides, it is found that possible long‐range magnetic order induced by Fe diffusion into the GGG spacer may give rise to interlayer exchange coupling and enhance magnon transmission, leading to an increased MJR at low temperatures, whereas paramagnon‐mediated spin transport is proposed to dominate at elevated temperatures. Our results provide new insights into spin/magnon transport in epitaxial magnon junctions and offer a promising strategy for developing high‐performance magnonic devices.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: Design Principles of Bioadhesives for Wearable and Implantable Bioelectronics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Bioadhesives have emerged as essential materials for bridging the interface between medical devices and biological tissues, offering conformal, biocompatible, and minimally invasive adhesion in complex physiological environments. Their importance is particularly evident in wearable and implantable bioelectronics, which demand stable integration with dynamic and often moist tissues. Wearable devices must maintain long‐term skin contact while accommodating motion and sweat, whereas implantable systems require secure fixation to internal organs and tissues while limiting inflammation and fibrosis. In both applications, conventional adhesives fall short in achieving reliable adhesion under such conditions. Bioadhesives address these challenges by enabling intimate tissue‐device contact and supporting mechanical and electrical performance. However, the design of bioadhesives for biomedical electronics involves multifaceted requirements, including interfacial toughness, energy dissipation, biological compatibility, and environmental adaptability. This review organizes the field through a design‐evaluation‐integration framework that links interfacial chemistry and energy dissipation with physiological constraints, application‐matched evaluation, failure‐mode feedback, and device‐level performance. We also discuss practical considerations related to biodegradation, anti‐swelling, immune response, and delivery strategies for difficult‐to‐access sites. By identifying application‐dependent trade‐offs among adhesive, mechanical, electrical, and biological requirements, this framework supports the comparative assessment of bioadhesives for wearable and implantable electronic systems.

title: Decoding Tumor Metabolic Dysregulation Through Single‐Cell Analysis Informs the Inverse Design of Therapeutic Nanozymes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Single‐node interventions often fail against tumor metabolic networks due to dynamic compensation and pathway redundancy, necessitating synergistic, multi‐node strategies. However, translating high‐dimensional single‐cell omics into physicochemical parameters for materials design remains a major challenge. Herein, a cross‐scale inverse design paradigm for therapeutic nanozymes is proposed that maps single‐cell metabolic demands onto quantum‐chemical descriptors. Using hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as a model, integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and metabolic flux analyses revealed a triple vulnerability network involving lactate accumulation, focal hypoxia, and oxidative stress imbalance. Guided by first‐principles calculations and multiparameter screening based on reaction energy barriers and Bader charge transfer, 260 candidate materials were evaluated. This screening identified a nitrogen–phosphorus dual‐coordinated gold single‐atom nanozyme (APNC) with exceptional lactate oxidase (LOX)‐, catalase (CAT)‐, and peroxidase (POD)‐like activities and strong piezoelectric polarization. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that APNC remodels the HCC microenvironment by depleting lactate and alleviating hypoxia, thereby disrupting glycolysis and triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). APNC‐mediated piezocatalytic therapy achieved 95% tumor inhibition in vivo. This inverse design strategy bridges single‐cell metabolic profiling and atomic‐scale material engineering, establishing a versatile framework for precision nanozyme development across tumors and metabolic disorders.

title: Ion‐Access Engineering for High‐Performance Vertical Organic Electrolyte‐Gated Transistors
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic electrolyte‐gated transistors (OEGTs) are promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic systems owing to their low‐voltage operation and strong ionic–electronic coupling. However, in vertical OEGTs, which offer higher current densities and faster switching, the semiconductor channel is often shielded from direct electrolyte contact, limiting ionic accessibility and resulting in inefficient gate coupling and slow switching dynamics. Here, we introduce a photolithography‐free ion‐access strategy for vertical OEGTs, combining femtosecond laser micropatterning with inkjet‐printed solid‐state electrolytes. Laser‐defined pores penetrating the top electrode and semiconductor layer create direct ionic pathways to the channel region, significantly enhancing ionic–electronic coupling. As a result, the devices exhibit more than two orders of magnitude enhancement in transconductance (up to 9.17 mS), over 300‐fold enhancement in current density reaching 51.8 A cm
                    −2
                    , and an on/off ratio approaching 10
                    7
                    , together with accelerated switching dynamics compared to devices without pore structures (>6‐fold reduction in turn‐on time constant). This ion‐access engineering strategy is compatible with multiple organic semiconductor materials and provides an effective structural strategy for overcoming ionic transport limitations in vertical OEGTs. Moreover, array‐level demonstrations and a proof‐of‐concept NARMA2 reservoir computing task (NMSE = 0.107) further illustrate the scalability and neuromorphic application potential of this platform.

title: A Scalable Protrusion‐Targeted Electrolyte Enables 500 Wh Kg −1 Lithium Metal Batteries With 500‐Cycle Stability
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The development of lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is severely impeded by limited cycle life arising from irreversible lithium dendrite growth. Herein, we design a scalable, protrusion‐targeted electrolytes to achieve industrial‐scale LMBs through retarding the formation of dendritic lithium embryos. The site‐selective‐blocking molecules preferentially adsorbs onto protrusive sites of lithium deposition, which inhibits the local lithium deposition rate to block dendrite initiation. More importantly, the abundant polar functional groups of adsorbed molecules induce directional enrichment of anions, achieving passivation repair of fresh dendritic lithium. This synergy of selective adsorption and interfacial repair effectively inhibits the self‐amplifying growth of lithium dendrites, thereby mitigating continuous electrolyte consumption. An 8 Ah‐level pouch cell with 500 Wh kg
                    −1
                    delivers an impressive capacity retention of over 80% after 525 cycles. Furthermore, we show large‐scale production of electrolytes for preparing industrial‐scale LMBs. This design offers a viable approach for long‐life LMBs at an industry compatible scale.

title: A Perspective on Continuous Superlattices and Device‐by‐Design Pathways Toward Electrically Driven Perovskite Lasers and Cooperative Emission
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Halide perovskites are emerging optical gain media; however, electrically assisted lasing is currently prohibited by Joule heating, ion migration, injection imbalance, high‐density non‐radiative recombination, and contact‐related optical losses. This Perspective summarizes recent progress on optically pumped micro‐ and nanolasers and identifies materials and resonator architectures relevant to electrical operation. We further distinguish current‐induced lasing from superradiance and superfluorescence stemming from cooperative exciton emission. We then consider continuous perovskite superlattices containing experimentally verified periodic electronic potentials, as a proposed platform for controlling carrier transport, energetic disorder, and optical transitions. If such architectures also preserve coherent and spectrally homogeneous exciton synchronization, they may support transient cooperative emission. Steady‐state bad‐cavity cooperative lasing is a distinct, more demanding objective requiring common‐mode synchronization and repumping that sustains collective coherence. By separating established demonstrations from proposed materials concepts, we outline a materials‐ and device‐design roadmap toward electrically driven perovskite lasers and cooperative light sources.

title: Biomimetic Optically Encoded Hydrogel Fiber Enables Simultaneous Olfactory‐Mechanosensory Perception for Robotic Plume Tracing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Dynamic odor plumes encode gas identity and airflow transport as coupled spatiotemporal cues, requiring olfactory‐mechanosensory fusion perception for intelligent robotic navigation in vision‐denied environments. Yet current olfactory‐mechanosensory systems typically rely on separated sensing units, limiting co‐localized mechanochemical discrimination. Here, we report a biomimetic flexible optical fiber (BFOF) comprising a coaxial hydrogel fiber with distributed, self‐assembled odor‐sensitive metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) on its exterior, enabling simultaneous decoding of wind vectors and olfactory cues within a single compact optical architecture. Inspired by the spatially integrated mechanoreceptors and chemoreceptors in ant antennae, the BFOF employs conformal MOF‐hydrogel interfaces to enhance evanescent‐field coupling without compromising receptor activity or waveguiding, partitioning multidimensional airflow attenuation and odor fluorescence into separable optical channels for low‐crosstalk olfactory‐mechanosensory fusion. Therefore, it achieves high sensitivity, fine directional selectivity, and fast temporal response across a wide range of airflow conditions. It identifies 16 individual gases, 96 mixtures, and the physiological states (unripe, ripe, overripe, and rotten) of 8 fruits with high accuracy. Coupled with a lightweight machine‐learning framework, this work establishes rapid, precise, and closed‐loop anemotactic navigation and multi‐target odor tracing in complex three‐dimensional (3D) spaces, offering a compact optical sensing platform for embodied robotic olfaction beyond static gas classification.

title: Gigacycle Fatigue Resistance and Cyclic Phase Separation in Metastable Nanocrystalline Cu–Ag Alloy Thin Films
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanocrystalline metals derive their exceptional strength from a high density of grain boundaries (GBs), but under cyclic loading those same boundaries are unstable, driving abnormal grain growth that seeds fatigue cracking. Solute‐mediated grain boundary stabilization is shown here to extend nanocrystalline fatigue life by orders of magnitude. A metastable nanocrystalline Cu–42 at.% Ag alloy thin film survives 1.2 billion cycles at strain amplitudes exceeding 1.1%. To our knowledge, no other metallic thin film has shown gigacycle fatigue resistance at such extreme strain amplitudes, while comparison with literature data requires care given differences in testing conditions. A combination of microresonator‐based very‐high‐cycle fatigue testing, electron microscopy, and atomistic simulations reveals a composition‐dependent transition in the governing mechanism. In dilute Cu–3Ag, solute clusters kinetically pin interfacial disconnections and slow boundary migration, extending fatigue life but not preventing eventual failure via abnormal grain growth. In contrast, concentrated Cu–42Ag exhibits stable grain boundaries for over a billion cycles. Fatigue damage is ultimately associated with a previously unreported fatigue‐induced phase separation: strain‐enhanced transport decomposes the metastable solid solution into semi‐coherent Cu‐ and Ag‐rich domains. Solute‐stabilized nanocrystalline alloy thin films thus offer a route to gigacycle fatigue resistance in microdevices, and cyclic phase separation emerges as a distinct damage mode.

title: Li–B–Mg Composite Foils With a LiB 0.88 Microrod Array Enable Ultrathin Self‐Supporting Lithium Metal Anodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Ultrathin self‐supporting lithium foils (USSLFs, ≤50 µm) are highly desirable for high‐energy‐density batteries, as eliminating current collectors enhances energy density and reduces material costs. However, the intrinsic mechanical vulnerability of metallic Li remains a critical barrier to both the fabrication and long‐term cycling of USSLFs. Herein, we develop a Li‐rich Li–B–Mg composite foil (LBM) through sequential melt alloying followed by post‐solidification thermomechanical processing, yielding a dense and interconnected LiB
                    0.88
                    microrod array with LiMg and MgB
                    2
                    lithiophilic phases within the Li‐rich matrix. This architecture enables large‐area (>170 cm
                    2
                    ) self‐supporting foils down to 15 µm while preserving a high Li content. During cycling, the microrod array redistributes local stress and restrains deformation, preserving the internal architecture and accessibility of lithiophilic sites. These sites, in turn, favor Li accommodation within the electrode interior, suppressing surface Li accumulation and alleviating local stress concentration. This self‐sustained coupling between stress regulation and lithiophilic guidance supports stable cycling for over 5000 h in symmetric cells using 50 µm LBM foils with about 10% thickness expansion, while 15 µm foils cycle for over 500 h at a depth of discharge of about 37.4%. This work advances the design of practical USSLFs for high‐energy lithium metal batteries.

title: Pulsed Electrosynthesis of Conformal High‐Entropy Metallic Glass Skins for Durable Industrial Water Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐entropy metallic glasses (HEMGs) combine compositional diversity with a grain‐boundary‐free amorphous topology, making them attractive as electrocatalytic interfaces. However, their synthesis remains challenging because multicomponent transition‐metal alloys favor crystallization over vitrification. Here, we report a room‐temperature pulsed electrosynthesis (PES) strategy that kinetically traps HEMG skins, defined here as continuous, conformal HEMG coatings approximately 100 nm thick, directly on practical electrodes under ambient aqueous conditions. Using crystallization‐prone FeCoNiMo, millisecond ultrahigh‐current pulses induce burst multimetal nucleation while suppressing diffusion‐mediated crystallization, enabling programmable control over crystallinity, morphology, and composition. The resulting chemically homogeneous, grain‐boundary‐free skins suppress localized corrosion and structural collapse, favoring spatially distributed surface reconstruction. FeCoNiMo HEMG‐skinned electrodes sustain alkaline hydrogen evolution at 2 A cm
                    −2
                    for over 1,300 h, whereas crystalline counterparts fail within approximately 200 h. As bifunctional electrodes in an anion‐exchange‐membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), they achieve 1 A cm
                    −2
                    at 1.706 V and operate for 1,200 h, outperforming the Pt/C‖IrO
                    2
                    benchmark under identical conditions. Roll‐to‐roll upgrading of commercial Ni mesh (0.5 m × 2 m) further demonstrates fabrication scalability. These results establish PES‐driven HEMG skinning as a practical route for integrating metastable amorphous multimetal interfaces with electrode architectures.

title: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. Here, we report a uricase-like platinum-nitrogen-carbon nanozyme (Pt-N-C-NH
                    3
                    ) that redirects UA oxidation from a two-electron pathway toward a four-electron pathway. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. The sensor exhibits a wide linear range of 50.00 to 1000.00 μM and a detection limit of 15.86 μM, while maintaining 97.57% signal stability against reductive interferents. This work demonstrates that atomic-level coordination engineering enables programmable control over reaction pathways in artificial enzyme systems, thereby facilitating robust biosensing in complex biological environments.

title: Structural insights into light harvesting and photosystem II evolution in the basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride
source: Science Advances
abstract:
The basal streptophyte
                    Mesostigma viride
                    represents a critical evolutionary transition toward land plants, yet the molecular basis of its ancestral light-harvesting strategy remains elusive. Here, we present a 2.25-angstrom resolution cryo-EM structure of the
                    M. viride
                    PSII-LHCII-LHCP supercomplex, revealing a unique C
                    2
                    S
                    2
                    M
                    p2
                    L
                    p2
                    -type architecture. Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. At the periphery, the complex features a specialized antenna module in which two ancestral LHCP monomers flank CP29. These ancestral antenna proteins bind an unusually high number of carotenoids, with seven carotenoids per subunit, and extensively incorporate marine-type keto carotenoids, siphonaxanthin, and siphonein, throughout the complex, thereby broadening absorption in the blue-green region. The canonical LHCII trimer exhibits a distinctive chlorophyll
                    b
                    macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond ultrafast energy transfer component. Together, these findings provide a high-resolution molecular framework for an evolutionary intermediate that combines high-capacity aquatic light harvesting with structural features potentially relevant to photoprotection during the transition toward terrestrial life.

title: High‐Efficiency Perovskite‐Organic Tandem Solar Cells Enabled by Perovskite Crystallization Optimization and Metal‐Free Interconnecting Layer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Perovskite‐organic tandem solar cells (PO‐TSCs) offer a promising route toward high‐efficiency and cost‐effective photovoltaics by combining wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with narrow‐bandgap organic solar cells. Nevertheless, achieving high‐performance PO‐TSCs still faces key challenges: open‐circuit voltage (
                    V
                    OC
                    ) loss in the WBG perovskite sub‐cell and optoelectrical loss at the interconnecting layer (ICL). Here, we incorporate 4‐nitrophenethylamine hydrochloride (4N‐PEACl), a functional additive bearing a strong electron‐withdrawing group (‐NO
                    2
                    ), into the WBG perovskite precursor solution to modulate crystallization kinetics and passivate bulk defects. This additive significantly improves crystallinity and phase stability, suppresses non‐radiative recombination and enhances charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the optimized 1.85 eV WBG single‐junction PSC achieves a champion efficiency of 19.79%, with
                    V
                    OC
                    increasing from 1.349 to 1.388 V. Furthermore, the optimal PO‐TSC achieves an efficiency of 27.10% with an ICL of PCBM/AZO/SnO
                    2
                    /PEDOT:PSS/Ph‐4PACz. This work highlights the efficacy of ‐NO
                    2
                    ‐functionalized molecules in improving WBG perovskite film quality and provides new design strategy for low‐cost but effective ICLs in PO‐TSCs.

title: Preadipocyte-Derived Decellularized Extracellular Matrix-Functionalized Three Dimensionally Printed Scaffolds Regulate Vascularized Adipose Tissue Regeneration via Modulation of Selected Paracrine Factors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The clinical efficacy of soft tissue reconstruction is severely hindered by unpredictable graft resorption and inadequate vascularization. Traditional synthetic implant scaffolds offer mechanical support, with limited bioactivity for adipose tissue regeneration. In this study, we developed a “three-in-one” bioinstructive platform (dPCL) integrating structural support, signal induction, and immunomodulation by functionalizing a 3D-printed polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) derived from 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. The obtained dECM-functionalized scaffold provided essential biochemical cues. In vitro assays demonstrated that dPCL significantly enhanced preadipocyte adhesion and adipogenic differentiation. Besides, the dECM-functionalized scaffold was found to modulate the secretion of selected paracrine factors, markedly upregulating the secretion of adiponectin, VEGF, and IL-10, which facilitated cell differentiation and robust endothelial network formation. In vivo evaluation in a murine subcutaneous model confirmed that dPCL scaffolds effectively supported the formation of stable, well-vascularized adipose tissue. Furthermore, the dECM-functionalized scaffold enhanced the recruitment and accumulation of proregenerative M2 macrophages, maintaining an M2-dominant tissue microenvironment that facilitated graft integration. In summary, current findings demonstrate that integrating cell-specific dECM with 3D-printed scaffolds creates a multifaceted bioactive platform that overcomes the critical barriers of vascularization and metabolic integration, presenting a highly promising strategy for functional soft tissue regeneration.

title: Scalable Hybrid Photocatalysts for Visible‐Light Degradation of Waterborne Organic Contaminants
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic micropollutants in aquatic environments pose persistent risks to human health and ecosystems, yet current remediation technologies face scalability, stability, and secondary pollution challenges. Here, we report a visible‐light‐responsive photocatalyst prepared by covalently immobilizing benzothioxanthene imide (
                    BTI
                    ), a ton‐scale industrial dye, onto macroscopic oxide supports (Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    , zeolites). The densely grafted
                    BTI
                    forms H‐aggregates that suppress radiative decay, enabling efficient interfacial electron transfer, generating hydroxyl (OH
                    •
                    ) and superoxide (O
                    2
                    •–
                    ) radicals without co‐catalysts. This system achieves degradation of a diverse range of contaminants (e.g., dyes, pharmaceuticals, and agrochemicals) into CO
                    2
                    and CO under low‐intensity visible light, with no detectable activity loss over 12 months of continuous operation. A pilot‐scale flow reactor packed with millimeter‐sized
                    BTI
                    ‐functionalized beads demonstrates efficient treatment of real dye mixtures under ambient conditions, highlighting scalability, recoverability, and compatibility with decentralized wastewater treatment. This work establishes a sustainable, modular platform for water purification, particularly in resource‐limited settings.

title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Kondo insulators are paradigmatic strongly correlated materials, traditionally found in f-electron compounds. They originate from the hybridization between itinerant conduction electrons and localized magnetic moments, which opens a gap in the electronic spectrum. Two-dimensional moiré systems provide a new route to flat bands with strong electron correlation, which host localized moments at half filling. Here we report signatures, based on local conductivity measurements using microwave impedance microscopy, of a Kondo insulator in a moiré superlattice of monolayer WS2 / bilayer WSe2, in which one WSe2 layer carries flat moiré bands and the other dispersive ones. When both layers are partially doped with two holes per moiré unit cell in total, an insulating state appears when the moiré band contains less than one hole. The insulator becomes metallic above a certain threshold magnetic field, evidence for the singlet nature of the Kondo insulator, and the observed behavior is reproduced by a periodic Anderson model. Our results open a route to simulating Kondo physics in tunable moiré systems.

title: Electronic Modulation Engineering of Pt-Modified TiO2 Nanotube-Confined Co Catalyst for Efficient Low-Temperature Catalytic Oxidation of CH3SH
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Methanethiol (CH3SH) is a typical malodorous volatile organic pollutant, and its efficient low-temperature catalytic degradation remains both an urgent priority and a formidable challenge in odor abatement. Herein, we leveraged the unique curved surface architecture of titanium dioxide nanotubes ((TiO2 NTs) and developed a targeted electronic-modulation strategy in which cobalt (Co) species were confined within the nanotube channels via vacuum impregnation, followed by the photodeposition of platinum (Pt) onto the outer surface as an electron-withdrawing layer to yield a composite catalyst (Co@TiO2 NTs-Pt). Catalytic performance evaluations showed that Co@TiO2 NTs-Pt exhibits excellent low-temperature activity toward CH3SH oxidation, achieving approximately 95% conversion at room temperature and enabling complete oxidation of sulfur-containing intermediates at even lower temperatures than those required with Co@TiO2 NTs. Comprehensive characterization indicated that depositing Pt on the exterior surface enhances the electron-deficient environment within the nanotube cavity and induces surface lattice distortion, thereby raising the oxidation state of the confined Co species and increasing the concentration of oxygen vacancies. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further confirmed that this electronic-modulation strategy significantly strengthens CH3SH chemisorption and activation on the catalyst surface. Furthermore, in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) elucidated the reaction pathways governing CH3SH oxidation over the catalyst surface. Overall, this study deepens the understanding of electronic confinement effects in TiO2 NTs and provides a theoretical basis and technical guidance for designing advanced catalysts for the efficient low-temperature abatement of malodorous organic pollutants.

title: Selective aromatization of polyolefins by temporal decoupling from cracking
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cracking of polyolefins is a prerequisite for their selective conversion over microporous zeolites to value-added small molecules such as monocyclic aromatics. However, cracking and aromatization often proceed concurrently, creating an intrinsic accessibility-selectivity conflict that limits aromatic yield and productivity. This paper describes a strategy that temporally decouples polyolefin cracking from selective aromatization in one-pot with tandem catalysts. This strategy delivers an aromatic yield of ca. 60.3 wt% within 0.5 h at 380 °C from postconsumer polyolefins over 40 consecutive cycles, corresponding to an aromatic space-time yield of 11 g gcat−1 h−1, more than twofold higher than reported values of ≤ 5 g gcat−1 h−1. Kinetic and mechanistic studies reveal that self-pillared pentasil zeolite rapidly and processively cracks polyolefins to small olefinic intermediates below 320 °C, enabling temporal decoupling of low-temperature cracking from higher-temperature aromatization through distinct dominant kinetic windows. Process modeling further suggests favorable economic potential and life-cycle greenhouse-gas emissions 26% lower than fossil-based aromatics production and 66% lower than incineration. This work establishes temporal decoupling as a reaction-engineering strategy for reconciling polymer accessibility with micropore-controlled selectivity in plastic upcycling.

title: Multidimensional Protein-Based Antimicrobial Materials: Construction, Mechanisms, and Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bacterial contamination and associated infections remain persistent threats to global public health. Proteins, as renewable biomacromolecules with diverse functional groups, programmable hierarchical structures, and favorable biocompatibility, have emerged as versatile building blocks for antimicrobial materials. Through self-assembly, amyloid-like aggregation, interfacial engineering, and chemical or physical functionalization, proteins can be constructed into zero-dimensional (0D) micro/nanoparticles, one-dimensional (1D) fibers, two-dimensional (2D) films and coatings, and three-dimensional (3D) hydrogels, aerogels, and sponge scaffolds. Dimensional architecture extends beyond morphological classification: it governs active-site exposure, interfacial contact, mass transport, mechanical properties, and antimicrobial-agent retention and release, thereby determining bactericidal activity, resistance to bacterial adhesion, and antibiofilm performance. Nevertheless, the relationships connecting dimensional construction, interfacial structure, antimicrobial mechanism, and application-specific performance remain fragmented. This review therefore adopts dimensionality as the central framework for critically examining the structural design, assembly, and functionalization of protein-based antimicrobial materials across 0D–3D architectures. Particular emphasis is placed on how dimensional features regulate the antimicrobial mechanisms involving membrane disruption, cell-wall hydrolysis, reactive oxygen species generation, physical bacterial trapping, controlled antimicrobial release, and resistance to bacterial adhesion. Recent advances in the applications of these antimicrobial materials, categorized by their dimensional architectures, are further evaluated across biomedicine, food preservation, functional textiles, and agriculture in relation to their operating environments and functional requirements. Finally, challenges concerning mechanistic validation, long-term stability, scalable manufacturing, biological safety, and application-specific evaluation are critically discussed to identify barriers to practical implementation and future directions for technological translation. Emerging opportunities in AI-assisted protein and peptide design, precise interfacial engineering, and multifunctional integration are further highlighted to guide the rational development of next-generation protein-based antimicrobial materials.

title: Interfacial Integration of Cross-Kingdom Membranes Establishes a Rechargeable Energy Cascade
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Engineering modular adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-mediated energy transduction pathways from the bottom up faces two key bottlenecks: first, detergent-dependent reconstitution typically impairs protein activity and energetic coupling efficiency due to disrupted native lipid environments and randomized protein orientation; second, physically separated ATP production and consumption modules suffer from severe diffusional ATP losses and inefficient intermodule cascade coupling. To address both limitations, we report a programmable, nondestructive strategy to construct a high-performance artificial organelle—the “chrometabosome”—through orthogonal peptide-driven fusion of photosynthetic chromatophores and energy-consuming erythrosomes. Bypassing detergent solubilization and reconstitution, this strategy not only preserves membrane proteins in their native lipid environment and functional state but also colocalizes ATP-producing and ATP-consuming modules within a single nanoscale compartment. This colocalization reduces the dependence of ATP utilization on intervesicle transport, producing a 3- to 4-fold kinetic enhancement at lower vesicle concentrations relative to nonintegrated controls. This light-rechargeable system offers a modular framework for versatile biohybrid energy nanosystems.

title: Strain-induced correlated metallic phase in 1T-TaS2
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenide 1T-TaS2 has long been considered a prime example of a Mott insulator driven by strong electron correlations. However, this view has been recently challenged by proposals which favor a band insulating state arising from interlayer dimerization. This ongoing debate opens a frontier in 1T-TaS2 research focusing on stacking order, and raises a fundamental question with broad implications for two-dimensional materials: can electronic phases be engineered by actively tuning interlayer coupling? Here, using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that uniaxial strain drives 1T-TaS2 from its insulating charge-density-wave phase into a stable metallic phase. This metallic phase, distinct from hydrostatic-pressure-induced or non-equilibrium hidden phases, emerges via a strain-induced rearrangement in the interlayer stacking of the Star-of-David charge order, effectively disrupting interlayer dimerization. Furthermore, the emergent metallic phase exhibits a significant quasiparticle mass renormalization, a hallmark of strong electron correlations, indicating its correlated nature and proximity to a Mott instability. This finding necessitates a re-evaluation of the interplay between structural and strong correlations in 1T-TaS2. The present results establish uniaxial strain as a powerful method for tuning the interlayer coupling, opening pathways for exploring quantum phases inaccessible under ambient conditions.

title: Critical raw material intensity of electricity generation technologies: A probabilistic and multicriteria approach applied to the European Union
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do not support robust comparisons between electricity generation technologies for decision-making in energy planning and policy. In this context, the present study proposes a probabilistic multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework to assess and rank electricity generation technologies according to their material requirements in t/MWh. It incorporates at least one method from each major MADM family and includes strategies to enhance resilience against rank reversal. Material consumptions are aggregated into satisfaction or criticality indices, while Monte Carlo simulation captures uncertainty and variability in consumption, lifetimes, and operational conditions. The methodology is applied to the EU including eight electricity generation technologies (wind, solar PV, solar CSP, hydro, biomass and waste, nuclear, coal, and natural gas) and 33 raw materials. Despite minor differences among MADM methods, the framework consistently converges on a ranking in which wind and solar PV are the most material-critical technologies, followed by solar CSP; coal, natural gas and nuclear occupy intermediate positions; biomass and waste, and hydro are the least critical alternatives. These findings highlight that EU decarbonisation strategies must be complemented by targeted raw material policies, including diversification of supply, recycling, material substitution, and strategic planning, to ensure that the transition to renewable electricity is not only low-carbon but also materially resilient and secure.
