title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Mammalian biology unfolds over time, within tissues and organs opaque to our eyes and instruments. We applied DNA Typewriter, a sequential molecular recorder, to record the cell lineage of a mouse over nearly 2 weeks of development. From one embryo, we reconstructed a time-calibrated, parsimony-supported, zygote-rooted phylogeny of 1.28 million transcriptionally profiled cells. A burst of editing unequivocally marks the daughters of the first cleavage, which serve as inline replicates. We quantified clonal dominance arising during gastrulation. Tree siblings share cell type far above chance; heterotypic siblings mark terminal differentiations. Temporal sweeps of clade co-occurrence recover a dated hierarchy of cell type couplings; imputed labels for internal nodes recapitulate known state paths. A lineage-anchored ontogeny of mammalian development, long out of reach, is coming into view.

title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo–electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor’s ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Wernicke’s area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke’s area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke’s area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

title: Physicochemical microenvironments within biomolecular condensates govern reaction kinetics beyond mass-action effects
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cells utilize phase separation to compartmentalize biochemical reactions within biomolecular condensates. Although these compartments can enhance reaction rates by concentrating reactants, how they modulate kinetics beyond mass-action effects remains poorly understood. Here, using spontaneous protein ligation as a model reaction, we examined how the physicochemical microenvironment within condensates modulates reaction kinetics. We systematically analyzed condensates formed by folded PRM–SH3 scaffolds and intrinsically disordered proteins (LAF, TAF, and FUS). We designed a proximity-sensitive client probe to assess excluded-volume-driven increases in effective reactant concentration. In parallel, we characterized condensate hydrophilicity and associated changes in water activity, identifying these properties as additional key kinetic determinants. Together, our findings elucidate how effective concentration and hydrophilicity jointly regulate biochemical reactions within condensates.

title: Cryo-EM provides insight into how the Staphylococcus aureus IsdH receptor removes hemin from the hemoglobin:haptoglobin complex
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Staphylococcus aureus
                    extracts hemin from human hemoglobin (Hb) to overcome host-imposed iron limitation. How it recovers Hb-bound hemin from the hemoglobin:haptoglobin (Hb:Hp) complex, the major circulating form of Hb outside red blood cells, remains unclear. Here, we use cryo-electron microscopy, biophysical measurements, and solution kinetics to define how the
                    S. aureus
                    IsdH surface receptor extracts hemin from Hb:Hp. A 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of Hb:Hp bound by full-length IsdH reveals that its N-terminal NEAT domain (N1) anchors it to αHb, whereas its downstream N2N3 extraction unit engages βHb to remove its hemin. The receptor engages Hb:Hp differently than isolated Hb, because N-linked glycans on haptoglobin bias the extraction unit toward βHb, sterically occluding its access to αHb while still permitting engagement by N1. Kinetic assays show that IsdH actively accelerates hemin release from Hb:Hp. Three-dimensional variability analysis indicates that this likely occurs via a dynamic interface in which receptor motions reposition the extraction unit relative to βHb, collectively supporting a model in which IsdH transiently perturbs the F-helix to promote hemin extraction. Alignment of that model with a previously determined CD163:Hb:Hp structure shows how IsdH may disrupt Hb:Hp recognition by macrophage and monocyte CD163 receptors, helping to explain how it may hinder clearance of Hb:Hp from circulation. In aggregate, these results help define the structural basis for hemin extraction from Hb:Hp and how IsdH may subvert receptor-mediated clearance of the Hb:Hp complex.

title: Morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Modern western legal and criminal justice theories assume that punishment should deter criminalized behavior by introducing costs that reduce its expected utility, but, empirically, punishment often has weak effects on rates of crime and recidivism. Here, we hypothesize that when people are motivated to engage in criminalized behavior for moral reasons, they show diminished sensitivity to punishment. We demonstrate our hypothesis across 10 correlational, experimental, and economic game studies with participants drawn from the general population as well as participants with criminal backgrounds. Studies 1 to 3 draw on federal data of over 30,000 offenders and find that participants’ estimates of moral motives for crime predict higher recidivism while estimates of material motives predict the opposite. Studies 4 to 8 use judgment studies and find that morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment across a diversity of crime types, when motives are manipulated but actions are kept constant, persist for different types of consequences, and are unique to moral motivation. Studies 9 and 10 employ economic games and find that when players take money from others for moral reasons, they are less deterred by the imposition of fines. Implications for systems of punishment, offender psychology, and restorative justice approaches are discussed.

title: Lactate-rich tumor employs the KAT5–HIF1α axis to modulate the activity of the hypoxia pathway and facilitates tumor progression
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Substantial evidence shows that hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF1α) up-regulates glycolytic enzymes and promotes lactate production, which contributes to “Warburg Effect.” Nevertheless, the impact of lactate or lactylation modification on hypoxia signaling pathways within the tumor microenvironment remains largely unclear. Here, we report that lactate can induce the upregulation of hypoxia pathway activity in a HIF1α-dependent manner. We identified that KAT5 as a lysine lactyltransferase of HIF1α and the “writer” responsible for lactylation at HIF1α K389, K460, K674, and K682, and HDAC2 as a HIF1α de-lactylase. The lactylation-deficient mutant of HIF1α (HIF1α
                    4KR
                    ) reduced HIF1α stability, along with down-regulating hypoxia-mediated angiogenesis, metastasis, apoptosis, and glycolysis. Mechanistically, the HIF1α
                    4KR
                    mutant enhances the binding of HIF1α to von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor protein (VHL), facilitating its degradation. MG149, a KAT5 inhibitor, can enhance the efficacy of anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)-based combination immunotherapy in a murine model by suppressing hypoxia pathway activity in tumor cells and potentiating the cytotoxic function of CD8
                    +
                    T cells. Clinically, lactylated HIF1α and KAT5 are up-regulated in breast cancer tissues compared with adjacent tissues. Notably, elevated levels of HIF1α lactylation and KAT5 expression were observed in resistant cancer specimens from triple-negative breast cancer patients who had undergone neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Our results indicate that the tumor lactate microenvironment promotes the formation of the tumor hypoxic microenvironment by hijacking and lactylating HIF1α, and the KAT5–HIF1α Kla axis presents a promising therapeutic target for hypoxic tumors.

title: Coevolving gene networks underlying a phenotypic syndrome revealed via integrating comparative genomic and microevolutionary analyses
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Complex adaptive traits often comprise interacting, coevolving phenotypes that together for a syndrome that is shaped by multiple genetic loci. While using intraspecific variation is an established approach for investigating syndromes, such polymorphism typically captures only a subset of syndrome traits. Diapause, an alternative developmental pathway that evolved independently in many species to synchronize life cycles with resource availability, exemplifies this challenge. While subsets of this essential phenotype have long been studied at a single species level, the genomic basis of the full diapause syndrome remains poorly understood. This paucity of insights has fueled a long-standing debate about how life cycle synchronization evolves and whether convergent phenotypes employ shared mechanisms. Using a comparative genomic analysis spanning diverse diapause transitions in butterflies, we identified a large network of coevolving genes unique to diapausing species. The network is composed of functional modules spanning circadian regulation, metabolism, and cell cycle control. We tested whether this macroevolutionary scale network predicts microevolutionary dynamics, hypothesizing that this network is the polygenic architecture underlying the diapause syndrome. Analyses revealed that allelic variation in the diapause network is significantly enriched in signatures of local adaptation across latitudes, but only in diapausing species. Thus, we empirically show that diapause evolves through modular, coevolving gene networks, components of which impact intraspecific variation in diapause. Using this integrative perspective on a complex phenotype opens a horizon of inquiry for understanding seasonal adaptation across evolutionary scales, while demonstrating the power of integrating comparative genomics with microevolutionary dynamics to dissect complex phenotypic syndromes.

title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron–containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

title: Linear plasmids mediate antimicrobial resistance gene transfer between environmental bacteria and hospital-adapted enterococci
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
As animal hosts adapted to land,
                    Enterococcus
                    species diverged from a common ancestor shared with
                    Vagococcus
                    species by acquiring genes essential for survival and transmission in the exposed arid environment. In addition to their intrinsic ruggedness, human-associated enterococci now frequently exhibit multidrug resistance, largely driven by the accumulation of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) on mobile genetic elements (MGEs). However, the source of these resistance elements, their diversity in natural reservoirs, and their risks remain unclear. To investigate clinically relevant ARGs and their associated MGEs in a wastewater-impacted environment, we examined environmental vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) recovered from a polluted urban river in Hanoi, Vietnam. Whole-genome sequencing of VRE isolates revealed multidrug-resistance pELF-type linear plasmids harboring a fluoroquinolone resistance gene (
                    qrtA
                    ) encoding a major facilitator superfamily transporter. The
                    qrtA
                    gene appears to have originated on
                    Vagococcus
                    -related chromosomes and may have been mobilized by IS
                    1216E
                    -associated MGEs.
                    Vagococcus
                    genomes show strong associations between ARGs, IS
                    1216E,
                    and plasmids related to those in enterococci, and conjugation experiments demonstrated that pELF-type linear plasmids can transfer between
                    Enterococcus
                    and
                    Vagococcus
                    without major fitness costs. Comparative analysis of pELF-type linear plasmids, together with database mining, identified
                    qrtA
                    -positive clinical isolates from geographically separated regions in Asia and Europe, indicating that
                    qrtA
                    is not confined to a single local setting. These findings highlight the need for coordinated international One Health surveillance of ARG and MGE dynamics, including emerging determinants such as
                    qrtA
                    , together with interventions to limit their spread.

title: Serine–glycine lipid homeostasis in Bacteroidota modulates membrane stability and host interactions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Lipid 1256 (L1256) is a large complex aminolipid produced by members of the phylum
                    Bacteroidota
                    that is formed by addition of a phosphatidic acid (PA) moiety to the precursor aminolipid, L654. Studies have shown that L1256 is enriched in diseased gingival tissues, linking synthesis of this aminolipid to sites of chronic inflammation. Given that PA is involved in membrane rearrangements and L654 is a known Toll-like receptor 2 ligand associated with health, we hypothesized that synthesis of L1256 could influence outer membrane vesicle (OMV) biogenesis and innate immune responses. Here, PG1647 was identified as a lipid synthase required for biosynthesis of L1256 in
                    Porphyromonas gingivalis
                    . Loss of PG1647 abolished L1256 and related minor species, while impairing membrane stress resistance and intracellular survival. PG1647 loss also increased OMV production and enhanced the proinflammatory activity of bacterial cells and OMVs. These phenotypes occurred without broad transcriptional changes, supporting lipid remodeling as a central driver. Structural and biochemical analyses supported a phospholipase D-like role for PG1647. Complementation with the
                    Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
                    homologue BT3978 restored L1256 production in
                    P. gingivalis
                    and partially rescued associated phenotypes, suggesting functional conservation among the host-associated
                    Bacteroidota
                    . Additional studies determined that many species in the phylum
                    Bacteroidota
                    carry a similar functional enzyme, further indicating the importance of this class of enzyme for
                    Bacteroidota’s
                    physiological functions. Altogether, these findings show that loss of PG1647 alters OMV biogenesis, inflammatory activity, and host-associated fitness in the endogenous oral pathogen,
                    P. gingivalis
                    , linking these phenotypic changes to PG1647-dependent aminolipid remodeling.

title: Causal dynamic resonance reduces false positives in detecting causality
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Many dynamical systems in nature, such as brains and weather systems, are highly nonlinear and complex. Determining information flow among the components that make up these dynamical systems is challenging. If the components are the result of a common process or become synchronized, causality measures typically fail. We previously introduced Cross-Dynamical Delay Differential Analysis, a nonlinear method for assessing causal influence, along with a complementary approach for dynamical similarity between time series data, Dynamical Ergodicity Delay Differential Analysis. Here, we show that “Causal Dynamic Resonance (CDR)” further improves the false positive rejection rate by adding white noise to the data, without perturbing the underlying dynamical system. This is followed by a study of CDR in coupled Rössler systems, where ground truth interactions are known and in invasive intracranial electroencephalographic data from drug-resistant epilepsy patients undergoing presurgical monitoring.

title: Preemptive solving of future problems: Multitask Preplay in humans and machines
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Humans can pursue a near-infinite variety of tasks, but typically can only pursue a small number at the same time. We hypothesize that humans leverage experience on one task to preemptively learn solutions to other tasks that were accessible but not pursued. We formalize this idea as “Multitask Preplay”, an algorithm that replays experience on one task as the starting point for “preplay”—counterfactual simulation of an accessible but unpursued task. Preplay is used to learn a predictive representation that can support fast, adaptive task performance later on. When implemented within deep reinforcement learning, it predicts human generalization to novel tasks more accurately than traditional planning and predictive representation methods across grid-worlds and a 2D Minecraft domain. Additionally, Multitask Preplay improves an artificial agent’s ability to generalize to new environments sharing task co-occurrence structure. These findings demonstrate that Multitask Preplay is a scalable theory of human counterfactual learning and generalization; endowing artificial agents with this capacity can significantly improve their performance in challenging multitask environments.

title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

title: Lipid-induced Caveolin1 lipid droplet trafficking is associated with lipid droplet growth
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Caveolae are 50 to 100 nm sized plasma membrane invaginations involved in cellular lipid uptake and lipid accumulation. Several caveolin1 and cavin1 mutations are associated with human lipodystrophy. Previous research identified caveolae proteins at lipid droplets, although their specific cellular function at lipid droplets is not understood. Here, we show that extracellular dietary lipids like oleic acid and cholesterol shift caveolae at the plasma membrane to highly spherical invaginations and induce the internalization of caveolin1. Within 3 h of lipid treatment, caveolin1 accumulates specifically to lipid droplets. Correlative fluorescence Focused Ion Beam – Scanning Electron Microscopy and split-APEX proteomics revealed that this localization occurs in the absence of intact caveolar vesicles but caveolin1 alone. Mechanistically, caveolin1 trafficking to lipid droplets is regulated by EHD2 at the plasma membrane, is dynamin independent, and proceeds via EEA1- and Rab5-positive endosomes within 1 h of oleic acid treatment. Lipid droplet accumulation of caveolin1 is independent of lysosomal activity. Functionally, caveolin1-enriched lipid droplets exhibit a significant increase in size, demonstrating that caveolin1 is critical for lipid droplet growth. Notably, the deletion of the central caveolin1 β-barrel (Cav1-F160X), a mutation identified in lipodystrophy patients, abolished caveolin1 lipid droplet trafficking and lipid droplet growth. Taken together, our results show that dietary lipids trigger caveolin1 internalization and accumulation at lipid droplets and a caveolin1-dependent lipid droplet growth, thereby providing an initial mechanistic basis for the lipodystrophic phenotype associated with caveolin1 mutations.

title: Counterions, polarization, and pore hydration relay drive ion permeation through hydrophobic pore formed by the MERS coronavirus E protein
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Hydrophobic pores are generally expected to exclude ions because the large desolvation penalty associated with ion transfer cannot be compensated within a nonpolar environment. The envelope (E) protein of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) presents a striking exception, conducting cations with high efficiency despite forming a predominantly hydrophobic pore. To resolve this apparent paradox, we combine finite-temperature string simulations with additive and polarizable force fields to determine the minimum free-energy pathways for ion permeation through the MERS E channel. The simulations reveal a cooperative permeation mechanism in which transient counterion association, localized pore hydration, and electronic polarization jointly reduce the desolvation penalty. Rather than acting as passive spectators, counterions transiently chaperone the permeating cation before dissociating within the channel, thereby lowering the energetic cost of charge desolvation while preserving net ionic conductance. Explicit electronic polarization further reshapes the pore hydration landscape and cation–
                    
                      
                        π
                      
                    
                    interactions, leading to substantially reduced free-energy barriers and a permeation mechanism that is in substantially better agreement with experiment. These results suggest that efficient ion transport through hydrophobic pores arises from the cooperative interplay between electrostatics, polarization, and hydration rather than complete pore wetting, providing both a mechanistic framework for MERS E protein function and a general physical principle for ion transport through biological and synthetic hydrophobic nanopores.

title: Authentic structure of the CCHFV RNA–nucleoprotein complex at near-atomic resolution
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) poses a major public health threat without approved vaccines or antivirals. Its ribonucleoprotein (RNP) is essential for replication, but its native architecture and RNA packaging remain elusive. Here, we combine AI-based structural prediction with cryo–electron microscopy to resolve the native structure of the CCHFV RNP purified from CCHFV-infected cells. We report a 3.87 Å structure of a single-turn RNP, and local refinement yielded a 3.55 Å structure of two adjacent NP protomers with continuous RNA. This represents the highest-resolution authentic RNP structure reported among segmented negative-strand RNA viruses (sNSVs), and provides the structural basis for CCHFV RNP assembly. Together with mutational analyses, these findings define the molecular basis of RNA encapsidation and NP oligomerization in the native CCHFV RNP. Our findings provide a hybrid structural framework integrating AI and experimental approaches for understanding genome organization in sNSVs and offer a foundation for future antiviral development.

title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.

title: Co-translational surveillance of nascent polypeptides times circadian rhythms in Drosophila
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) ensures proteostasis by actively degrading aberrant translation intermediates on stalled ribosomes, yet its physiological role in gene regulation remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that
                    Drosophila
                    circadian clocks employ RQC to sustain 24-h behavioral rhythms. RNA interference-mediated depletion of RQC components in circadian pacemaker neurons impaired free-running locomotor rhythms. In particular, the loss of
                    Caliban
                    (
                    Clbn
                    ) function in clearing 60S-associated faulty polypeptides led to weak but long-period rhythms in adult locomotor activity. These behavioral phenotypes were accompanied by delayed accumulation of the core clock protein PERIOD (PER), most evidently in pigment-dispersing factor-expressing clock neurons, and dampened structural plasticity of their axons.
                    per
                    heterozygosity exaggerated CLBN depletion-induced period lengthening, whereas overexpression of the PER-associating factor TIMELESS blunted this effect.
                    Clbn
                    deficiency in
                    Drosophila
                    S2R+ cell cultures increased the generation of prematurely terminated PER species, particularly when PER translation is high, and sensitized full-length PER to phosphorylation-dependent decay. These findings support PER as a clock-relevant RQC substrate, providing a mechanistic link between translation flux, co-translational surveillance, and circadian timekeeping.

title: Transformer-Enhanced Hybrid Model-Data Driven Approach for Power Deficit Estimation in Low-Inertia Power Systems
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Accurate real-time estimation of power deficits following disturbances is critical for maintaining grid stability in low-inertia power systems with high renewable energy penetration. This article presents a transformer-enhanced hybrid model-data-driven framework that synergistically combines physical interpretability with adaptive learning for real-time power deficit estimation. The approach consists of two co-designed components: first, an improved model-driven module employing sliding-window Gauss–Newton frequency fitting to extract center-of-inertia rate-of-change-of-frequency for generator-side estimation; and second, a novel Transformer with multihead frequency attention mechanism that captures complex nonlinear load-side dynamics through multiscale feature extraction. The hybrid framework incorporates scenario-specific adaptive correction mechanisms that learn optimal fusion weights, preserving interpretability while enhancing accuracy. Validated on the Chinese Society for Electrical Engineering—Frequency Stability benchmark and a provincial receiving-end power grid, both with high renewable-energy penetration, the proposed framework outperforms representative deep-learning baselines [long short-term memory (LSTM), long short-term memory–convolutional neural network (LSTM-CNN), and LSTM-CNN with an attention mechanism (lstm-CNN-Attention)] in mean relative error, maximum relative error, and root-mean-squared error. The framework delivers reliable real-time performance for practical grid-control applications.

title: Co-Optimizing Frequency Security and Battery Degradation via Adversarial Robust Optimization in Power Systems With High Renewable Penetration
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, power systems are characterized by lower inertia and greater uncertainty, thereby increasing the risk of frequency violations. To address this challenge, this article proposes an adversarial max–min robust scheduling framework that co-optimizes dynamic frequency security and battery energy storage system (BESS) degradation in renewable-rich power systems. First, a two-stage analytical frequency-response model is developed to capture both unsaturated and reserve-limited primary frequency response dynamics and to derive explicit constraints on the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and frequency nadir. In addition, a rainflow-based BESS cycle-aging model is established to quantify the lifetime impact of repeated frequency-support operation. To solve the resulting nonlinear max–min problem efficiently, deep neural network surrogate models are embedded through a big-M reformulation and combined with a combinatorial cutting algorithm to obtain a tractable mixed-integer linear programmingformulation. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed framework maintains the RoCoF within 0.15 Hz/s and the frequency nadir at or above 49.4 Hz throughout the operating horizon. Moreover, explicitly accounting for BESS degradation reduces the monthly degradation cost from USD 65 000 to USD 36 000, corresponding to a 44.6% reduction, while maintaining a comparable overall system operating cost.

title: A Feasible Solution for Conflicting Assessment Indices of Active Suspension Systems: Pareto-Based Output-Feedback Optimal Control
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Although numerous advanced active suspension control methods have been developed, few studies address the inherent conflict between ride comfort and road holding. Most existing approaches focus on single-objective optimization without considering these two conflicting performance indices simultaneously and achieving a compromise between them. This article presents a Pareto-based output-feedback optimal control method for active suspension systems, where the Pareto front can be obtained to achieve a tradeoff between ride comfort and road holding. Specifically, two independent value functions associated with ride comfort and road holding are designed. Then, an output algebraic Riccati equation (OARE) is derived to avoid using full system states and observer techniques. To obtain the optimal solution of the OARE, an adaptive learning algorithm is designed to ensure the convergence to the optimal solution. Considering the conflicting nature of ride comfort and road holding, the Pareto dominance principle is employed, by which the Pareto-based output-feedback optimal control gain can be calculated based on the derived optimal solution of the OARE. Hence, the Pareto front can be characterized to provide a series of feasible solutions for different active suspension control requirements. Theoretical analysis is conducted to prove the existence of the Pareto-based output-feedback optimal control gains. Simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: DSR-ICMark: A Framework With Detail Sensitivity and Fidelity Restoration for IC Marking Inspection in Large-FOV PCBA Images
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Accurate reading of integrated circuit (IC) markings is essential for product traceability and quality analysis in industrial visual inspection. In printed circuit board assembly images captured with a large field of view, substantial character-scale variation, highly regular structured backgrounds, and degraded marking details jointly hinder accurate detection and recognition. We propose DSR-ICMark, a unified framework for IC marking detection, restoration, and recognition. The detail-sensitive adaptive detector builds multiresolution representations and selects effective scales based on local content, preserving fine details while suppressing background interference. The character-balanced map loss combines region-level importance with prediction confidence to adaptively calibrate spatial supervision and focus optimization on sparse foregrounds and challenging regions. A lightweight character restoration network reconstructs damaged strokes and local details.The recognition-guided fidelity optimization strategy uses downstream task supervision to guide restoration, reducing the effects of image degradation on feature discriminability. Extensive benchmarks show that DSR-ICMark matches or outperforms representative detection, recognition, and spotting models, with fewer parameters and faster inference. Industrial deployment tests show that DSR-ICMark achieves the lowest end-to-end latency, supporting its potential for practical IC marking inspection.

title: Reliability Analysis of RIS Assisted DF Cooperative SWIPT for Industrial IoT-Enabled Vehicular Communication Systems
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT)-enabled vehicular communication has become an important infrastructure for smart transportation, intelligent logistics, and industrial mobility applications. In such scenarios, vehicles, roadside units, sensors, and infrastructure nodes are interconnected to support reliable information exchange, while the limited energy supply of distributed vehicular devices remains a critical bottleneck. To enhance the reliability and energy sustainability of IIoT-enabled vehicular networks, this article investigates a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted decode-and-forwardcooperative simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system. Considering cochannel interference at both the relay and destination nodes, the outage performance of the proposed system is analyzed under time switching relay (TSR) and power splitting relay (PSR) protocols. Semianalytical outage expressions are evaluated by Gauss–Laguerre quadrature and verified by Monte Carlo simulations. Furthermore, the impacts of the number of RIS reflecting elements, outage threshold, Nakagami-m fading parameter, time switching factor, power splitting factor, and energy conversion efficiency are examined. Numerical results show that RIS deployment improves reliability under the considered mean-interference benchmark, whereas the relative performance of TSR and PSR depends on the allocation and channel parameters.

title: Interoperability of Electric Drive Models Using HELICS
source: IEEE Transactions on Energy Conversion
abstract: Accurate modeling and simulation are essential for the effective design, testing, and evaluation of electric machine systems. However, existing models often face interoperability challenges due to differences in programming languages (e.g., C, MATLAB, Python) and the separation of components such as inverters and controllers across diverse environments. These challenges are amplified by the growing use of advanced simulation platforms like Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) and Controller-HIL, which require repeated adaptations for compatibility. This paper presents a HELICS-based co-simulation framework that enables seamless coordination among heterogeneous tools and models, providing a unified platform for integrating and testing electric drive models regardless of their origin. The approach is demonstrated through the co-simulation of an inverter-fed permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) drive under speed control, showcasing flexible reuse of existing models, and offering a scalable, modular solution for collaborative and repeatable electric drive system testing and development.

title: Optimal Scheduling of Smart Meter Measurement Reporting Intervals for Distribution System Monitoring and State Estimation
source: IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources has intensified uncertainty in distribution systems, making distribution system state estimation essential for situational awareness and advanced control. Although smart meters improve state-estimation observability, bandwidth limitations often preclude continuous high-rate streaming, and utilities therefore rely on fixed reporting intervals. Such fixed-rate reporting induces asynchronous sampling and sample-and-hold effects, leading to time-skew error and degraded estimation accuracy. This paper proposes a time-skew-error-based sensor-scheduling framework that optimizes the reporting interval of each meter under an explicit communication budget equal to that of fixed-interval baselines. The method models reporting-induced time-skew-error statistics as interval-dependent uncertainty and selects reporting intervals that minimize the resulting error without increasing the total number of uploads. To enhance robustness under nonstationary load and distributed-energy-resource dynamics, the framework integrates distribution-shift detection for periodic re-optimization and event-triggered transmissions to capture photovoltaic-generation and electric-vehicle transients. Case studies on a real-world 127-bus feeder show that, under the same communication budget, the proposed approach consistently reduces the root-mean-square errors of both nodal injection measurements and estimated voltage magnitudes relative to standard fixed-interval reporting across multiple baseline intervals. Under the representative 15-min fixed-interval baseline, the active/reactive-power measurement root-mean-square errors are reduced by 65.18%/66.47% and the voltage-magnitude root-mean-square error by 54.67% in the solar/electric-vehicle-rich scenario; corresponding reductions of 29.37%/33.36% and 27.89% are retained when independently measured 1-min household data are used.

title: From Forecasts to Feasible Decisions: Network-Constrained Demand Response with Projection-Integrated Decision-Focused Learning
source: IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid
abstract: In distribution network operation, forecasting models are widely used to support demand response (DR) optimization subject to distribution-network constraints. However, minimizing statistical prediction errors does not necessarily improve downstream operational decisions, particularly in strongly constrained networks where small forecast deviations may trigger constraint violations or infeasibility. This paper proposes a feasibility-aware decision-focused learning framework for network-constrained DR in distribution systems. Instead of training forecasting models solely using mean squared forecasting error, downstream operational objectives under feasible conditions are incorporated into model fine-tuning. A differentiable feasibility projection layer is integrated into the learning pipeline to map forecast-based candidate solutions to admissible operating points, allowing for stable gradient propagation to refine the forecasting model toward improved forecasts for constraint-consistent decisions. Numerical case studies on representative distribution networks demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially reduces infeasible outcomes compared with conventional two-stage predict-then-optimize pipelines while achieving a more favorable trade-off between statistical forecasting accuracy and operational performance.

title: Decentralized Stability-Constrained Optimal Power Flow for Inverter-Based Power Systems
source: IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
abstract: Future inverter-dominated power systems feature higher variability and more stressed operating conditions, which motivates the consideration of stability in operational settings. Existing approaches to stability-constrained OPF often rely on eigenvalue calculation, global model information, or dynamic evaluation inside optimization formulation, which are computationally intensive and difficult to scale. To the best of our knowledge, this paper develops the first decentralized stability-constrained OPF framework for inverter-based power systems. The key novelty lies in embedding a class of algebraic decentralized small-signal stability criteria that admit tractable representations in steady-state variables and are therefore suitable for optimization. These decentralized stability conditions are based on local voltage differences and network parameters, which enable a clear theoretical and practical economic interpretation of the stability contribution from each inverter. We define a Nodal Stability Shadow Price (NSSP) for each inverter, and characterize the role of these stability constraints through their associated shadow prices, enabling a nodal interpretation of their economic impacts. It is proved that under active-power-only objectives in lossless networks, binding stability constraints may occur but will admit zero shadow prices if all other operational constraints are inactive. Most importantly, we reveal the importance of considering the opportunity cost of reactive power for inverter-based resources (IBRs) that have limited capacity. When reactive power costs are considered, stability constraints can carry strictly positive shadow prices and admit meaningful economic impacts. Numerical studies on a two-bus system and the IEEE 39-bus system validate the proposed framework and illustrate how stability constraints influence optimal operational decisions and the impacts of control and network parameters such as the reactive power droop of grid-forming inverters.

title: Revisiting System Strength: A Unified Perspective on Stability and Robustness Via the Generalized Short-Circuit Ratio
source: IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
abstract: As inverter-based resources increasingly dominate modern power systems, system strength has become essential to secure operation. Conceptually, system strength characterizes the ability of a power system to withstand disturbances and maintain voltage waveforms, and is therefore inherently related to disturbance robustness. Existing studies, however, have primarily examined system strength from a small-signal stability perspective, while the analytical characterization of its stability boundary and its connection to disturbance robustness remain underdeveloped. This paper revisits system strength through the generalized short-circuit ratio (gSCR) and establishes a unified framework connecting eigenvalue-based stability analysis with singular-value-based robustness analysis. An analytical formulation of the critical gSCR (CgSCR) is derived, yielding an explicit small-signal stability criterion. Moreover, gSCR is shown to inversely characterize the worst-case amplification from current-injection disturbances to voltage responses, while the stability-derived CgSCR coincides with the critical point at which the robustness margin vanishes and the amplification becomes unbounded. These results reveal the intrinsic duality between the stability and robustness interpretations of system strength.

title: Adaptive Traveling Wave Detection Method for Transmission Line Fault Location Applications
source: IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery
abstract: This paper presents a new traveling wave (TW) detection method for transmission line (TL) fault location applications. The proposed solution defines an adaptive threshold from the statistical properties of the steady-state period of TW records, accounting for the effects of both Gaussian and non-Gaussian characteristics of real-world measurement noise. As a result, the user-defined setting process is no longer required, making the TW detection procedure more robust to the statistical variability of practical measurements and to errors associated with manual threshold adjustments. The validation of the proposed technique is carried out using a variety of real-world fault records taken from distinct manufacturers, whose distances were confirmed by the utilities' crew in the field. In each case, a classical double-ended TW-based fault location formulation is applied. The results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive strategy reliably detects the first fault-induced incident TWs, providing a settings-free and a manufacturer-independent methodology for post-fault analysis. Furthermore, statistical normality tests indicate that the steady-state noise cannot be fully described by a purely Gaussian model.

title: Privacy-Enhanced Federated Learning With Dynamic Reputation Consensus for Smart Grids
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Smart-grid services increasingly rely on distributed learning, but pooling regional load records, operating parameters, and topology information can violate privacy and critical-infrastructure constraints. Federated learning avoids direct data sharing, yet local updates remain exposed to gradient inversion, protected aggregation limits the observability of Byzantine poisoning and free-riding behavior, and static blockchain trust can be strategically manipulated. This article proposes privacy-enhanced federated learning with dynamic reputation consensus for secure smart-grid collaboration. Its protected update path combines integral affine-bijective grouped encoding, participant-specific masking, Paillier aggregation, and Shamir-based mask recovery to reduce encrypted payloads, retain a masking layer after private-key exposure when masks remain unavailable, and tolerate participant dropout. A benchmark-model-driven Euclidean distance and cosine similarity audit converts complementary magnitude and directional evidence into cross-round reputation for validator and leader selection and deposit-based incentives. Experiments on heterogeneous image benchmarks and two real-world load-forecasting tasks show stable utility under non-IID data, independent, mixed, and delayed strategic poisoning, and dropout rates up to 30%. In the evaluated LeNet-5 configuration, the encrypted payload decreases from 812.19 MiB for parameterwise Paillier-FedAvg to 7.96 MiB per client per round. Under the evaluated attack conditions, the key-exposure test yields distorted reconstructions. The election tests show close agreement between empirical and theoretical leader-election probabilities.

title: DGSM-Net: Doppler-Guided Completion and Statistical Matching for 4-D Radar Odometry
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Four-dimensional (4-D) millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar odometry has emerged as a promising alternative to vision- and LiDAR-based approaches due to its inherent robustness under adverse weather and illumination conditions. Nevertheless, 4-D radar point clouds are intrinsically sparse, geometrically ambiguous, and prone to spatial jump phenomena, which significantly degrade interframe registration reliability. To address these challenges, this article proposes DGSM-Net, a novel Doppler-guided and statistics-driven framework for robust 4-D radar odometry. Rather than treating Doppler measurements as ordinary auxiliary attributes or relying on deterministic feature matching, DGSM-Net uses Doppler-derived motion cues to guide geometric completion and models the matching process through local probabilistic inference under radar measurement uncertainty. First, to mitigate sparsity-induced geometric degradation, we develop a Doppler-guided geometric completion module, which aligns Doppler-derived motion cues with local geometric structures to enhance geometric completeness. Second, to alleviate spatial jump interference, we design a statistically guided robust matching module, which adopts NDT-based local probabilistic modeling and likelihood-guided confidence regulation to suppress unreliable correspondences. Extensive experiments on the public VoD benchmark, the self-collected dataset, and the long-range Snail-Radar dataset demonstrate that DGSM-Net achieves state-of-the-art odometry accuracy.

title: A Parallel Frequency Debiasing Network for Industrial Time Series Forecasting
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Accurate forecasting of industrial time series is crucial for planning subsequent tasks and generating economic benefits. Existing methods often pay excessive attention to low-frequency components with high energy while neglecting high-frequency information that contains critical details, exhibiting frequency bias. These high-frequency components contain short-term trends and potential patterns. To address this challenge, we propose a parallel residual network with independent spectral modeling for industrial time series forecasting (PrismTS). PrismTS adopts a multistack parallel architecture, where each stack serves as an expert for a specific frequency band. These stacks independently model future spectra, utilizing an internal dual-residual structure for deep feature extraction. This parallel data-flow design enhances the sensitivity to weak high-frequency signals and improves computational efficiency. Each stack contains a block-shared frequency scale to adaptively select valuable frequencies and suppress noise in the corresponding band. The hierarchical supervision strategy imposes band-specific constraints on each stack, mitigating the cross-band bias of high-energy signals caused by the global loss. Each stack serves as a frequency interpolator that maps low-resolution spectra to high-resolution predictions within the same frequency band, achieving superresolution reconstruction in the frequency domain. By quantifying the output of each stack, the contributions of different frequency bands to the final forecast can be analyzed, which effectively enhances interpretability. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that PrismTS achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and effectively mitigates frequency bias.

title: Magnetic Field Harmonic Modeling and Design of Fractional-Slot Dual-Winding Vernier PM Machines with Improved Torque and Power Factor
source: IEEE Transactions on Energy Conversion
abstract: In this paper, in order to further improve torque and power factor, a comprehensive magnetic field harmonic modeling and design approach is proposed for fractional-slot dual-winding vernier PM machine (FSDW-VPM). Firstly, analytical relationship among armature magnetic field harmonics, torque, and power factor is established. Then, the dominant armature harmonics contributing to torque and power factor characteristics are identified. Furthermore, to fully exploit dominant harmonics, the design concepts of dual-winding and hybrid-tooth are incorporated, enabling selective enhancement of dominant harmonics while suppressing those detrimental to the power factor. Finite element analysis (FEA) results show that the magnetic field harmonic modeling and design approach for synergistic harmonic improvement. Finally, a FSDW-VPM motor prototype is manufactured and tested to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the output torque and power factor.

title: Power Oscillation Suppression for Multi-Paralleled Grid-Forming Inverters via Hybrid Control
source: IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery
abstract: Grid-forming (GFM) inverters have grown ever more essential in power systems for their exceptional voltage and frequency support capabilities. However, due to the voltage based power regulation mechanism of traditional GFM controls, the active power regulation of multi-paralleled GFM inverters exhibits significant internal coupling, inducing undesirable power oscillation. Conventional control strategies such as increasing the virtual impedance for tackling this issue can partially suppress unfavorable interactions among multiple inverters but bring about negative effects including impairing voltage support capability. To overcome this limitation, this paper investigates the feasibility of suppressing power oscillation in grid-connected systems with multi-paralleled GFM inverters via a hybrid control based on current compensation, and further proposes targeted improvements with reference to the established active power loop coupling model. The proposed hybrid control scheme incorporates the advantages of current-based power regulation, and thus can effectively mitigate the power oscillation without compromising the closed-loop performance of the system. Finally, simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: A Benchmark Library for Distributed Power System Analysis and Optimization
source: IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
abstract: DPLib is an open-source benchmark library created to support research and development in distributed power system analysis and optimization. Unlike centralized tools such as MATPOWER and PGLib, no general purpose, reproducible data library package currently exists for distributed power system studies. DPLib, available at \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/DPLib.git}{GitHub}, fills this gap by providing 40 multi-region benchmark test cases ranging from 5 buses to 20758 buses, along with a graph-based partitioning toolkit that converts MATPOWER-compatible systems into distributed regional datasets. The toolkit generates standardized \texttt{.mat}, \texttt{.csv}, and \texttt{.m} files, regional MATPOWER version 2 cases, local and global bus mappings, generator and cost assignments, explicit inter-regional tie-line records, and bus-to-region partition maps. It supports unweighted, electrically weighted, and user-defined partitions, and is compared with METIS, KaFFPa, and an IPA-inspired baseline. DPLib also provides ADMM-based distributed DC and AC OPF solvers for validation. Numerical studies report partitioning sensitivity, centralized run times, distributed OPF iterations, run times, and optimality gaps. These results establish DPLib as a reproducible data layer for distributed power system research.
